Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interactions in the SU(2) gauge theory of the Shastry–Sutherland Dirac spin liquids

Yasir Iqbal Email: yiqbal@physics.iitm.ac.in Affiliation: Department of Physics, Indian Institute of Technology Madras, Chennai 600036, India
Abstract

We classify the fermion bilinears of the SU(2) gauge theory of the Shastry–Sutherland Dirac spin liquids under the spin–orbit-locked space group and treat the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions of SrCu2(BO3)2 at leading order in 1/N1/N and at one loop. At linear order DM can neither gap the spinons nor destabilize the SO(5) point above a scale T∗T^{*}. Symmetry forbids every local gauge-singlet fermion mass at any order. Among the singlet bilinears, the in-plane couplings induce only a conserved spin current of dimension exactly 2, which sets T∗=4​λ≃0.03T^{*}=4\lambda\simeq 0.03–0.170.17 K, and the out-of-plane coupling only a flavored spin-2 current, irrelevant at a unitary critical point. DM-induced Yukawa couplings start below 2%2\% of the one that bounds the pseudocritical window. In zero field, measured samples order above 11 K, at or above T∗T^{*}. Below T∗T^{*}, in a two-dimensional sample at the critical pressure, the Dirac cones reconstruct into a chirally protected dd-wave quadratic band touching whose only gauge-singlet gap channels are the two valence-bond components and the scalar chirality. A one-loop flow, with the gauge field screened by the band touching, ends at T∗⁣∗∼(0.03CLOSET^{**}\sim(0.03–OPEN0.1)​λ0.1)\lambda on a ray containing valence-bond order for the material’s exchange and for most random couplings, and otherwise on a gapped chiral ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} spin liquid. The DM bias between the two plaquette patterns is at most of order 10−410^{-4}, with a direction not fixed at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N), whereas non-magnetic quenched disorder couples a relevant random field to the plaquette doublet and none to the chirality. A field along [100][100] induces a (π,π)(\pi,\pi) Néel moment linear in the field; a field along [001][001] does not. This selection rule also holds in the dimer phase and is testable by 11B NMR under pressure.

I Introduction

Quantum phase transitions of two-dimensional antiferromagnets can fall outside the Landau–Ginzburg–Wilson paradigm when the critical degrees of freedom are fractionalized spinons coupled to emergent gauge fields [98, 97]. The Shastry–Sutherland (SS) lattice [103] is realized by SrCu2(BO3)2 [55, 83, 84], the most studied material candidate for such a transition [68]. Its crystal structure was determined by Smith and Keszler [108]. Under pressure its plaquette-singlet phase gives way to an antiferromagnet [133, 38, 67], also in applied fields [67, 105], and field-induced magnetization plateaus persist into the plaquette phase [42]. Field-tuned 11B nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) reports scaling near a proximate deconfined critical point [20], zero-field calorimetry finds a first-order transition with a bicritical point [39], and calorimetry in applied fields finds a specific heat linear in TT whose origin is open, fractionalized spin excitations being one possibility [40]. Between the plaquette and Néel phases of the SS model, numerical studies find a narrow gapless spin-liquid phase [130, 122, 18] (identified as a ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} Dirac spin liquid [73]), a weakly first-order transition [128], or a continuous one with emergent symmetry [70]. An infinite projected entangled-pair state (iPEPS) study extrapolated to infinite bond dimension places this phase at 0.785​(5)≤J′/J≤0.82​(1)0.785(5)\leq J^{\prime}/J\leq 0.82(1), compatible with a gapless spin liquid, entered from the plaquette phase by a weakly first-order transition and left continuously into the Néel phase, and attributes the differing conclusions of Refs. [128, 70] to limited bond dimension and, for Ref. [70], open boundaries [18]. A fermionic gauge theory unifies the SU(2) π\pi-flux state, the U(1) staggered-flux state U800 and the gapless ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} Dirac spin liquid Z3000 [73] within a single Higgs framework [27, 74], which carries over to the SS lattice the SU(2) gauge theory with adjoint Higgs fields constructed for the square-lattice antiferromagnet [101].

These field theories retain the SU(2) spin symmetry of the Heisenberg limit. The material has spin–orbit-induced Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions as its leading symmetry-lowering perturbation. The out-of-plane inter-dimer component D⟂′≃0.09D^{\prime}_{\perp}\simeq 0.09–0.180.18 meV [10, 94, 77] is the largest inter-dimer component [10, 77] and, by the symmetry analysis of Sec. II in agreement with Ref. [138], the only DM coupling that the structure allows above the buckling transition at Ts≃395T_{s}\simeq 395 K [112]. Below TsT_{s} in-plane components appear on the intra-dimer bonds, where they are the largest DM couplings [138, 63, 77], and on the inter-dimer bonds [14, 94, 77]. Together with symmetric anisotropies [79] they control the triplon splittings of the dimer phase [10, 30, 94, 79]. DM interactions have so far been included only in the dimer phase, at the dimer–plaquette transition by iPEPS [67], and in spin-wave analyses of the Néel phase [28, 8], and their absence from the theory of the deconfined scenario has been noted [19].

On the kagome lattice the out-of-plane DM component projects at linear order onto a time-reversal-even spin-triplet mass of the Dirac theory, the hexagon vector chirality, and was argued to induce 𝒒=0\bm{q}=0 order [45], as found by exact diagonalization above a finite Dc≃0.1​JD_{c}\simeq 0.1J [9] and variational Monte Carlo [44]. The DM-driven transition has been analyzed as one out of a ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} spin liquid of bosonic spinons [48]. The singlet projective symmetry groups carry over to zz-component triplet ansätze when each lattice operation also acts on spin [23], DM together with a spin polarization generates a net gauge flux through the unit cell [57], and DM drives a node-creating band inversion in a 1/91/9-plateau spinon state [65]. At a Higgs transition of the square-lattice Dirac spin liquid the critical Higgs fields break the emergent SO(5) with spin rotations intact [101, 100]. The effect of couplings that reduce the spin-rotation symmetry itself on the SS Dirac spin liquid has not been addressed.

The question matters for the SO(5) regime. In the theory of Ref. [27], with Nf=2N_{f}=2 Dirac fermions and Nb=2N_{b}=2 adjoint Higgs fields, the SO(5)-symmetric point at vanishing Yukawa coupling yy is left along the relevant yy. Its renormalization-group (RG) eigenvalue at large NN is ≃1.4\simeq 1.4, so the flow stays near that point over a pseudocritical window only for a small bare yy. The large-yy limit, a critical point without Lorentz invariance and with weakly broken SO(5), is the square-lattice theory of Ref. [101]. In the scenario of Refs. [125, 86] the flow instead passes slowly near a pair of complex fixed points. Emergent SO(5) then requires the rank-4 symmetric tensor to be effectively irrelevant, whereas the rank-2 tensor contains the tuning parameter and is relevant, as on the fuzzy sphere, where the rank-4 tensor has Δ=3.89​(3)\Delta=3.89(3) and the rank-2 tensor 1.456​(12)1.456(12) [137]. In the leading-order large-NN theory used here, whose tuning parameter is the Higgs mass, the symmetry-breaking part of the rank-2 tensor is irrelevant (Δ=3.46\Delta=3.46, Sec. VIII). Which operators DM induces, and with which dimensions, therefore decides whether spin–orbit coupling can act on the deconfined regime.

The companion Letter [52] states the symmetry results: time reversal and the spin–orbit-locked space group forbid every gauge-singlet fermion mass at any order in DM. At linear order the in-plane couplings enter the gauge-singlet bilinears only as the combination 𝒪DM=Jxx−Jyy\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM}=J^{x}_{x}-J^{y}_{y} (x|[100]x\parallel[100]) of conserved spin-current components, of dimension exactly 2 at the spin-rotation-invariant fixed point, and D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} only through a flavored spin-2 current, irrelevant at any unitary critical point; and a magnetic field activates the Néel moment selectively by orientation. The present paper derives these statements and follows their consequences, above the crossover scale T∗T^{*} set by 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM} and below it. The derivations rest on a complete classification of the fermion bilinears of the SS gauge theory, gauge-singlet and Yukawa, at zeroth and first gradient order, under the spin–orbit-locked space group, in which every lattice operation acts on spin through its axial-vector rotation. The Higgs fields are spin singlets, so the locked group acts on them as the unlocked one and their potential is unchanged. The classification agrees with the bilinear transformation tables of Ref. [27], and with those of Ref. [118] except for three time-reversal signs of the Néel-flavored gauge-adjoint currents, which we correct in Appendix A; our signs are used throughout, in particular for the Yukawa couplings of Sec. VI. The continuum symmetry action follows from projecting the lattice projective symmetry group (PSG) onto the Dirac subspace, the DM textures agree with Refs. [10, 94], and a lattice mean-field calculation confirms the operator selection. Appendix A states the conventions.

The main results of the paper are summarized below.

  1. 1.

    Crossover scale. The coefficient λ\lambda of 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM} is λ≃0.085​DΣ′\lambda\simeq 0.085\,D^{\prime}_{\Sigma} at mean field, with DΣ′D^{\prime}_{\Sigma} equal to 2\sqrt{2} times the in-plane inter-dimer DM component along the tetragonal axis of each bond, so that T∗=4​λ≃0.34​|DΣ′|T^{*}=4\lambda\simeq 0.34\,|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|, i.e. 0.030.03–0.170.17 K from the only density-functional-theory (DFT) calculation of the DM vectors, including the tabulated precision and a factor-1.71.7 prefactor uncertainty (Secs. II and IX.1).

  2. 2.

    Band touching below T∗T^{*}. Near the critical point the Dirac cones reconstruct into a chirally protected dd-wave quadratic band touching whose only gauge-singlet gap channels are the two valence-bond-solid (VBS) components and the scalar chirality (Sec. IX.2).

  3. 3.

    SO(5)-breaking perturbations above T∗T^{*}. At second order DM seeds the rank-2 SO(5) tensor, easy-axis from D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} and easy-plane from λ\lambda at mean field (Sec. VIII). The DM-induced Yukawa couplings to the critical Higgs fields come only from the intra-dimer DD, start at 6×10−46\times 10^{-4}–2×10−22\times 10^{-2} of the Yukawa coupling that bounds the pseudocritical window and, barring a cancellation among the Z3000 amplitudes, stay below it by at least that factor (Sec. VI).

  4. 4.

    Instabilities of the band touching. A Fierz-complete one-loop flow ends on a ray containing valence-bond order for most initial couplings, including the gauge-singlet ones and the exchange of the material, and otherwise on a gapped chiral ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} spin liquid with Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) Chern number ∓4\mp 4, at T∗⁣∗≃(0.03CLOSET^{**}\simeq(0.03–OPEN0.1)​λ0.1)\lambda (Secs. X.1 and X.2).

  5. 5.

    Plaquette selection. The DM correction to the plaquette pattern is a bias of at most of order 10−410^{-4} whose direction is not determined at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N), where the mixing of the SO(5)-singlet channel is solved but its Higgs sector is not controlled (Sec. X.3).

  6. 6.

    Magnetic fields. A field along [110][110] adds a valence-bond-imbalance mass at order B2​D2B^{2}D^{2}, and the in-plane component of a tilted field rounds a critical point on a scale that grows steeply as the scaling dimension of the Néel order parameter decreases (Sec. XI).

  7. 7.

    Disorder. Non-magnetic, time-reversal-invariant quenched disorder couples a relevant random field to the plaquette doublet and, to all orders in the disorder and in 1/N1/N, none to the chirality or the Néel channels. Random TcT_{c} is relevant at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N), a result that is not controlled at N=12N=12 (Sec. XII).

The U(1) descendant U800 carries exactly one symmetry-allowed monopole, the SO(5) singlet, with or without DM, so for U800 the symmetry argument excludes local masses but not confinement (Appendix N). The measurements that test these statements are an 11B NMR comparison of 𝑩|[100]\bm{B}\parallel[100] with 𝑩|[001]\bm{B}\parallel[001] at 2.42.4–2.82.8 GPa, calorimetry below T∗T^{*} near the critical pressure, a zero-field thermal Hall search below T∗⁣∗T^{**} (millikelvin scale or below under pressure) after field cooling, and an independent determination of the sign of D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}, which decides the direction of the DM plaquette bias only together with the SO(5)-singlet spectrum (Sec. XIII.3).

The paper is organized as follows. Section II sets up the model, the symmetry-allowed DM textures and the material parameters, and Sec. III constructs the spin–orbit-locked symmetry group of the continuum gauge theory. Sections IV–VII derive the results of the Letter: the operator content and the absence of gauge-singlet masses, the induced couplings and λ\lambda, the Higgs–Yukawa sector and node stability, and the dimension of the spin-2 current. Section VIII treats the second-order SO(5) anisotropies, Sec. IX the crossover scale and the band touching, Sec. X the instabilities of the band touching and the plaquette selection, Sec. XI the magnetic field, and Sec. XII quenched disorder. Section XIII compares the theory with experiment probe by probe, Sec. XIV lists the scope and limitations, and Sec. XV concludes. The appendices collect conventions, proofs and computational details. “Exact” denotes a statement fixed by symmetry, current conservation or unitarity. “Leading order” denotes O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) or one-loop results, and “estimate” denotes mean-field prefactors.

II Model and symmetry-allowed DM couplings

The Shastry–Sutherland model with DM interactions is

H^\displaystyle\hat{H} =Js​∑⟨i​j⟩□𝑺^i⋅𝑺^j+Jd​∑⟨i​j⟩dim𝑺^i⋅𝑺^j+∑bonds𝑫i​j⋅(𝑺^i×𝑺^j),\displaystyle=J_{s}\!\!\sum_{\langle ij\rangle_{\square}}\!\!\hat{\bm{S}}_{i}\!\cdot\!\hat{\bm{S}}_{j}+J_{d}\!\!\sum_{\langle ij\rangle_{\rm dim}}\!\!\hat{\bm{S}}_{i}\!\cdot\!\hat{\bm{S}}_{j}+\!\!\sum_{\rm bonds}\!\bm{D}_{ij}\!\cdot\!(\hat{\bm{S}}_{i}\times\hat{\bm{S}}_{j}), (1)

with Jd=JJ_{d}=J on the dimer bonds and Js=J′J_{s}=J^{\prime} on the square-lattice bonds. Throughout this paper JJ denotes the intra-dimer coupling. Several pressure studies label the two couplings the other way round [38, 39, 40, 20, 19, 127], and their numbers are quoted below in the notation of this paper. We use the conventions of Ref. [27], with square-lattice sites 𝒊=(ix,iy)\bm{i}=(i_{x},i_{y}) and a 2×22\times 2 unit cell with sublattices (mx,my)∈{A,B}2(m_{x},m_{y})\in\{A,B\}^{2}. The SS dimers lie along (1,1)(1,1), centered at (12,12)+2​𝒓(\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2})+2\bm{r} (material dimer AA, along the crystallographic [110][110] direction), and along (−1,1)(-1,1), centered at (32,32)+2​𝒓(\tfrac{3}{2},\tfrac{3}{2})+2\bm{r} (dimer BB). The square-lattice axes x^,y^\hat{x},\hat{y} correspond to the crystallographic [100],[010][100],[010] axes of SrCu2(BO3)2.

The material crystallizes in the tetragonal space group I​4¯​2​mI\bar{4}2m with CuBO3 layers stacked along cc [108]. Above Ts=395T_{s}=395 K the structure is I​4/m​c​mI4/mcm and the CuO4 plaquettes are planar. At TsT_{s} a second-order displacive transition buckles the layers [112]. The bending angle between neighboring CuO4 plaquettes, measured by single-crystal x-ray diffraction at ambient pressure, grows on cooling from zero at TsT_{s} to about 11∘11^{\circ} at 100100 K, the lowest temperature of that study [112]. High-resolution neutron powder diffraction from room temperature down to 22 K refines every data set in I​4¯​2​mI\bar{4}2m [121]. Below 3434 K, where the dimer singlet forms, the lattice shows a small negative thermal expansion and the bending angle decreases slightly, to about 10.9∘10.9^{\circ} at 22 K. The layers stay buckled, the CuBO3 layer is not a mirror plane for the dimers, and every DM component allowed by I​4¯​2​mI\bar{4}2m remains allowed [121]. We take the in-plane DM couplings introduced below to be those of the buckled structure and neglect this change of a few percent in the bending angle. Under pressure the tetragonal structure persists up to a continuous transition to a monoclinic phase, at 4.74.7 GPa at room temperature [71]. Between 2525 and 300300 K the onset of the monoclinic distortion stays between 4.04.0 and 5.05.0 GPa [134]. The plaquette phase and the antiferromagnet adjacent to it, studied at 1.81.8–33 GPa [20, 19, 39, 67] and up to about 44 GPa in Ref. [38], lie in the tetragonal phase, where the locked group I​4¯​2​mI\bar{4}2m applies; the antiferromagnetic order found above 44 GPa [133, 28, 127] lies at or above the monoclinic onset, which 11B NMR places near 44 GPa at low temperature [127]. Whether the plaquette phase itself lowers the tetragonal symmetry is not settled. Reference [124] finds at 2.42.4 GPa, in a cc-axis field of 77 T, a gradual loss of fourfold symmetry of the 11B magnetic shifts below about 3030 K, above its 3.63.6 K transition, and assigns it to an orthorhombic F​m​m​2Fmm2 symmetry of primarily magnetic origin, since the quadrupole couplings show no such loss. Reference [105] describes a tendency toward an orthorhombic distortion at intermediate pressure, and Ref. [5] expects no clear orthorhombic distortion of the crystal if the orientation of the weak intra-dimer bonds alternates between layers. Reference [71] attributes part of the anomalous in-plane compressibility to a reduction of the layer corrugation, which suggests that the in-plane DM couplings weaken under pressure. No low-temperature structure refinement under pressure quantifies this. The crystals contain inversion twins with volume fraction 0.50​(2)0.50(2) [112], and the two twin domains carry opposite signs of every in-plane DM component [113]. Inversion, which relates the two domains [112], leaves the magnetic field, the magnetization, the thermal Hall conductivity κx​y\kappa_{xy} and the NMR spectra unchanged, so these observables are the same in both domains. For the triplon thermal Hall effect, Ref. [113] notes that the two domains give κx​y\kappa_{xy} of the same sign. In that treatment the triplon dispersion and Berry curvature depend only on the square of the effective in-plane inter-dimer DM coupling.

DM textures from symmetry. With spin–orbit coupling, a lattice operation OO acts on spins through the axial-vector rule 𝑺→det(O)​O​𝑺\bm{S}\to\det(O)\,O\,\bm{S}, and a DM pattern {𝑫i​j}\{\bm{D}_{ij}\} is allowed if and only if 𝑫O⁡(i)​O​(j)=det(O)​O​𝑫i​j\bm{D}_{O(i)O(j)}=\det(O)\,O\,\bm{D}_{ij} for all locked operations. The allowed patterns form the null space of this condition on the space of bond vectors. For the high-temperature structure the mirror σh\sigma_{h} is itself a symmetry, so both OO and O​σhO\sigma_{h} act. In the buckled structure of space group I​4¯​2​mI\bar{4}2m the glide GxG_{x} and the fourfold rotation survive only combined with σh\sigma_{h}, while the diagonal mirrors σx​y,σx​y¯\sigma_{xy},\sigma_{x\bar{y}} act purely [112, 94]. The result is shown in Fig. 1 and Table 1. At high temperature a single coupling is allowed, the alternating out-of-plane inter-dimer D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}. Reference [10] proposed this pattern. It excluded the intra-dimer coupling by the approximate inversion center of each dimer, took the Cu plane as an approximate mirror plane, and neglected the in-plane inter-dimer components as smaller. Below TsT_{s} three further couplings appear: the staggered in-plane intra-dimer DD, perpendicular to each dimer, and the staggered and non-staggered in-plane inter-dimer components D′∥,sD^{\prime}_{\parallel,s}, D′∥,nsD^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns}. On the reference bond A1→B1A_{1}\to B_{1} we take 𝑫′=(−D∥,ns′,D∥,s′,D⟂′)\bm{D}^{\prime}=(-D^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns},D^{\prime}_{\parallel,s},D^{\prime}_{\perp}) in the frame (x^R,y^R,z^)(\hat{x}_{R},\hat{y}_{R},\hat{z}) of Ref. [94], related to ours in Appendix C. Supplementary Note 1 of Ref. [94] writes this vector as (−D∥,x′,D∥,y′,D⟂′)(-D^{\prime}_{\parallel,x},D^{\prime}_{\parallel,y},D^{\prime}_{\perp}), and the triangle rule stated there makes the yy component the staggered one. In our frame the same vector is (−(D∥,s′+D∥,ns′)/2,(D∥,s′−D∥,ns′)/2,D⟂′)\bigl(-(D^{\prime}_{\parallel,s}+D^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns})/\sqrt{2},\,(D^{\prime}_{\parallel,s}-D^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns})/\sqrt{2},\,D^{\prime}_{\perp}\bigr), as in Table 1. The patterns agree with the published figures arrow by arrow, up to the overall sign convention for DD (Appendix C).

Material parameters. The standard exchange set is J≃85J\simeq 85 K and J′≃54J^{\prime}\simeq 54 K, J′/J=0.635J^{\prime}/J=0.635 [84]. Reference [10] quotes the same JJ and J′J^{\prime}. Its 20-site exact diagonalization, compared with the measured ratio of the Raman-active singlet energy to the triplet gap, gives J′/J≃0.62J^{\prime}/J\simeq 0.62, and it extracts D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} at that ratio. Another fit gives J=71.5J=71.5 K with J′/J=0.603J^{\prime}/J=0.603 [62]. The iPEPS study of Ref. [105] uses J=81.5J=81.5 K at ambient pressure, a value between earlier estimates that agrees well with the observed onsets of the 1/4 and 1/3 plateaus. It takes J′/J=0.63J^{\prime}/J=0.63 from high-field magnetization data [76]. Those pulsed-field data, taken up to 118118 T with 𝑩|c\bm{B}\parallel c at 2.12.1–2.22.2 K, are best described by numerical results for the pure Shastry–Sutherland model at J′/J≃0.63J^{\prime}/J\simeq 0.63, and Ref. [76] states no value of JJ. First-principles values are J=7.3J=7.3 meV and J′=4.1J^{\prime}=4.1 meV [77].

The DM couplings are known with different degrees of certainty. The out-of-plane inter-dimer coupling D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} is the only DM coupling present above TsT_{s} and the largest inter-dimer anisotropy. Its raw observable is the zero-field splitting of the one-triplet electron spin resonance (ESR) lines for B|cB\parallel c, 8585 GHz =0.35=0.35 meV [88, 10]. The conversion to D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} depends on how J′J^{\prime} is treated. To lowest order in J′/JJ^{\prime}/J the splitting is δ⁡(q=0)=4​D⟂′\delta(q{=}0)=4D^{\prime}_{\perp} [10, 30]. The exact diagonalization of Ref. [10] finds that finite J′J^{\prime} reduces it to δ≃2.0​D⟂′\delta\simeq 2.0D^{\prime}_{\perp} at J′/J=0.62J^{\prime}/J=0.62, which gives D⟂′≃0.18D^{\prime}_{\perp}\simeq 0.18 meV, the value used here. Reference [30] notes that Ref. [10] estimates a reduction of the bandwidth by about a factor of two from quantum fluctuations. The triplon-hopping model of Ref. [94], which keeps terms linear in the DM couplings and takes JJ as the measured spin gap, has δ⁡(q=0)=4​|D⟂′|\delta(q{=}0)=4|D^{\prime}_{\perp}| and uses D⟂′=−21D^{\prime}_{\perp}=-21 GHz, i.e. |D⟂′|≃0.087|D^{\prime}_{\perp}|\simeq 0.087 meV, the magnitude also found by far-infrared spectroscopy [95]. The two estimates of D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} differ by a factor of two. The DFT value 0.100.10 meV [77] lies between them. The intra-dimer coupling is larger, with D/J=0.030D/J=0.030–0.0380.038 from the field-induced staggered magnetization seen by 11B NMR [63], i.e. D≃0.22D\simeq 0.22–0.280.28 meV, 0.220.22 meV from far-infrared spectroscopy [95], 0.31​(4)0.31(4) meV from the high-temperature ESR linewidth, assuming an in-plane inter-dimer component of 30%30\% of D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} [138], and 0.350.35 meV in DFT [77]. The in-plane inter-dimer components are the least constrained.
