IV Complete operator content

Operator content. The space of Hermitian gauge-singlet fermion bilinears at zeroth gradient order is 36-dimensional, the gauge-invariant subspace of the 120 Hermitian quadratic Majorana forms (Appendix B). It consists of the six masses and the 30 components of the conserved SO(5)-adjoint currents. The masses are the SO(5) vector nj=Tr⁡[𝒳¯​Γj​𝒳]n_{j}=\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\Gamma^{j}\mathcal{X}], two VBS and three Néel components, and the 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd flux singlet Tr⁡[𝒳¯​𝒳]\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mathcal{X}]. With 𝒳¯=𝒳†​γ0\bar{\mathcal{X}}=\mathcal{X}^{\dagger}\gamma^{0} these traces are Hermitian operators as written. The currents are Tr⁡[𝒳¯​γμ​Tj​𝒳]\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\gamma^{\mu}T^{j}\mathcal{X}] with the ten generators TjT^{j}. All ten SO(5)-adjoint scalars vanish identically by the Majorana reality condition (Appendix B). There is thus no quantum-spin-Hall-type mass Tr⁡[𝒳¯​𝒳​σa]\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mathcal{X}\sigma^{a}], no Tr⁡[𝒳¯​μx,z​𝒳​σa]\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mu^{x,z}\mathcal{X}\sigma^{a}] and no Tr⁡[𝒳¯​μy​𝒳]\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mu^{y}\mathcal{X}]. The complete transformation laws are given in Tables 2, 3 and 4.

Absence of gauge-singlet masses. Every existing mass is either 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd (the Néel components and the flux singlet) or odd under locked point-group elements (the VBS components, Table 3). Since DM preserves 𝒯\mathcal{T} and the locked space group, no explicit, symmetry-allowed local gauge-singlet fermion mass is generated at any order in the DM couplings. The locked space group alone already suffices: the locked glide together with σ^x​y\hat{\sigma}_{xy} leaves no mass invariant, and time reversal is an additional reason for the Néel and flux-singlet masses. This result concerns explicit local masses in the symmetric state and requires the full layer group. A shear strain along [110][110] lowers it and allows a VBS mass, and a magnetic field allows the masses of Sec. XI. Without these perturbations the Dirac nodes of the π\pi-flux state cannot be gapped by a gauge-singlet mass term. For U800 the same conclusion follows from the Φ3\Phi_{3}-Yukawa classification of Sec. VI, since the locked group admits a zeroth-order Φ3\Phi_{3} coupling only to a current and none to a mass. U800 is, however, a compact U(1) theory whose SO(5)-singlet monopole is invariant under both the unlocked and the locked group (Appendix N), so there the symmetry argument excludes local masses but not confinement by monopole proliferation. In the Higgs-condensed Z3000 phase, where the Yukawa sector adds gauge-adjoint bilinears, the nodes carry a chiral winding and can still disappear by pairwise annihilation if DM displaces them far enough, which this argument does not exclude; Sec. VI finds no such annihilation over the material-parameter range.

V DM-induced couplings

V.1 Zeroth gradient order

Of the 36 bilinears, DM can induce only those invariant under the locked group that its couplings preserve, and Tables 3 and 4 identify them. Without DM no operator is induced, as required. With D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} alone, under the high-temperature locked group and U(1)z, no operator is induced either, even without imposing 𝒯\mathcal{T}. With in-plane DM, under the buckled locked group, a single operator is generated,

𝒪DM=Tr⁡[𝒳¯​γx​𝒳​σx]+Tr⁡[𝒳¯​γy​𝒳​σy].\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM}=\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\gamma^{x}\mathcal{X}\,\sigma^{x}]+\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\gamma^{y}\mathcal{X}\,\sigma^{y}]. (7)

Here, and in the tables, the spin labels are related to physical axes by x→−xx\to-x (σlabelx=−Sx\sigma^{x}_{\rm label}=-S^{x}), which leaves the diagonal signs of the tables unchanged. In physical axes, with x|[100]x\parallel[100] and y|[010]y\parallel[010], Eq. (7) reads 𝒪DM=Jxx−Jyy\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM}=J^{x}_{x}-J^{y}_{y} up to an overall sign absorbed in λ\lambda. Two further current combinations are allowed without 𝒯\mathcal{T} and removed by it. 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM} is the spatial-diagonal, spin–orbit-locked component of the conserved spin currents. It acts as a constant non-abelian spin vector potential, Axspin∝SxA^{\rm spin}_{x}\propto S^{x} and Ayspin∝−SyA^{\rm spin}_{y}\propto-S^{y} in physical axes, with [Axspin,Ayspin]≠0[A^{\rm spin}_{x},A^{\rm spin}_{y}]\neq 0. A position-dependent spin twist removes it at linear order but not beyond, since the field strength [Axspin,Ayspin][A^{\rm spin}_{x},A^{\rm spin}_{y}] is of order λ2\lambda^{2} and gauge covariant, its norm being invariant (Sec. IX.1). Even at linear order the twist removes λ\lambda exactly only from spin-singlet observables, since it rotates the spin frame from site to site.

V.2 Gradient order

Genuine gradient couplings correspond to symmetric Majorana coefficient matrices, since antisymmetric ones are total derivatives of the zeroth-order bilinears. Beyond the two kinetic invariants the classification gives two structures for D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp},

OA\displaystyle O_{A} =Tr⁡[𝒳¯​σz​i​D↔0​𝒳],\displaystyle=\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\,\sigma^{z}\,\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}_{0}\,\mathcal{X}],
OB\displaystyle O_{B} =Tr⁡[𝒳¯​μy​σz​(γy​i​D↔x+γx​i​D↔y)​𝒳],\displaystyle=\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\,\mu^{y}\sigma^{z}(\gamma^{y}\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}_{x}+\gamma^{x}\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}_{y})\,\mathcal{X}], (8)

with D↔=12​(D→−D←)\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}=\tfrac{1}{2}(\overset{\rightarrow}{D}-\overset{\leftarrow}{D}) and σz\sigma^{z} the spin matrix. In the ψ\psi form of Eq. (4) they read OA∝ψ¯​i​D↔0​ψO_{A}\propto\bar{\psi}\,\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}_{0}\psi and OB∝ψ¯​μy​(γy​i​D↔x+γx​i​D↔y)​ψO_{B}\propto\bar{\psi}\mu^{y}(\gamma^{y}\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}_{x}+\gamma^{x}\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}_{y})\psi. They are spin-dependent velocity and tilt deformations that move but cannot gap the cones. For in-plane DM, the classification gives two further dimension-3 structures subleading to Eq. (7), six gradient invariants in total. The operator OAO_{A} is redundant. In the Euclidean conventions of Appendix O the off-shell identity ψ¯​i​D↔ν​ψ=12​εν​μ​c​∂μ(ψ¯​γc​ψ)+EOM\bar{\psi}\,\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}^{\nu}\psi=\tfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon^{\nu\mu c}\partial_{\mu}(\bar{\psi}\gamma_{c}\psi)+\text{EOM} holds, with the sign of the curl term reversed in the Minkowski signature of this section. The identity exhibits OAO_{A} as a total derivative of the conserved SzS^{z} spin current ψ¯​γc​ψ\bar{\psi}\gamma_{c}\psi plus equation-of-motion (EOM) terms, with no physical effect at linear order. The single physical dimension-3 operator induced by D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} is therefore OBO_{B}, the (x​y)(xy) component of the flavored spin-2 current Tr⁡[𝒳¯​ΓT​γ(μCLOSE​i​D↔​𝒳OPENν)]\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\,\Gamma_{T}\gamma^{(\mu}\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}{}^{\nu)}\mathcal{X}] with the flavor matrix ΓT=μy​σz\Gamma_{T}=\mu^{y}\sigma^{z}, a component of the SO(5) vector. Its ψ\psi form is 2​ψ¯​μy​γ(μCLOSE​i​D↔​ψOPENν)2\bar{\psi}\mu^{y}\gamma^{(\mu}\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}{}^{\nu)}\psi. It is a conformal primary, since the only descendants with its quantum numbers, derivatives of the currents with the flavor μy​σa\mu^{y}\sigma^{a}, vanish identically in the Majorana form. Its fate is computed in Sec. VII.

V.3 Lattice derivation of the induced coupling

The operator selection can be derived directly on the lattice. We Wick-decouple the DM term HDMH_{\rm DM} of Eq. (1) in the π\pi-flux and Z3000 ground states, using the ground-state correlations of one unit cell of a periodic lattice and summing the result over all lattice translations, and project onto the Dirac subspace. The projection yields zero for D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}, whose contributions cancel over the eight bonds of the cell, and zero for the intra-dimer DD on the π\pi-flux state, whose mean-field amplitudes connect only opposite sublattices of the square lattice while the dimer bonds join sites of the same sublattice. For the in-plane inter-dimer components it yields pure 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM}. The decoupling can be done in closed form (Appendix D). Let χ0=|⟨fi​σ†​fj​σ⟩NN|=0.23952\chi_{0}=|\langle f^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}f_{j\sigma}\rangle_{\rm NN}|=0.23952 be the nearest-neighbor (NN) singlet bond amplitude per spin (no sum over σ\sigma) of the π\pi-flux state in the thermodynamic limit (0.239630.23963 on the 16×1616\times 16 antiperiodic lattice of the finite-lattice calculations). Then

δ​ℒ\displaystyle\delta\mathcal{L} =λ​𝒪DM,λ=χ0​d2​2,\displaystyle=\lambda\,\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM},\qquad\lambda=\frac{\chi_{0}\,d}{2\sqrt{2}},
d\displaystyle d ≡DΣ′t,D′Σ≡D′∥,s+D′∥,ns,\displaystyle\equiv\frac{D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}}{t},\qquad D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}\equiv D^{\prime}_{\parallel,s}+D^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns}, (9)

in units of the spinon hopping tt, in agreement with the numerical projection. The staggered and non-staggered components contribute equally at this order. At mean-field order on the π\pi-flux state the intra-dimer DD enters only through the Higgs sector (Sec. VI). This follows from the sublattice selection rule χi​j=0\chi_{ij}=0 on the dimer bonds. Symmetry alone does not forbid it, since DD and D∥′D^{\prime}_{\parallel} transform identically under the locked group. Beyond mean field DD can renormalize λ\lambda. In the dimer phase, by contrast, DD and D′∥,sD^{\prime}_{\parallel,s} enter the triplon Hamiltonian of Ref. [94] at linear order only through the combination D~∥\tilde{D}_{\parallel}, and D′∥,nsD^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns} does not appear at that order (Sec. IX.1).

Coupling conventions. Throughout, dd denotes the lattice DM amplitude in units of tt, and λ=χ0​d/(2​2)≃0.085​d\lambda=\chi_{0}d/(2\sqrt{2})\simeq 0.085\,d is the continuum coefficient of 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM}. For the material, |DΣ′|≃0.16|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|\simeq 0.16–0.290.29 K (Sec. II) and the spinon hopping t≃20t\simeq 20–2222 K of Sec. IX.1 give |d|≃0.007|d|\simeq 0.007–0.0150.015 and λ≃10−3​t\lambda\simeq 10^{-3}\,t. The lattice calculations of Secs. X.2–XI use d=0.6d=0.6, about 40 to 80 times the material value, in order to resolve the quadratic band touching of Sec. IX.2 on finite grids. The sign of the plaquette harmonic b2b_{2} is the same for both signs of dd between 0.010.01 and 0.60.6 and for both in-plane textures (Appendix F). The field-selection signs are the same at d=±0.6d=\pm 0.6, and the Chern numbers also at d=0d=0, where the chirality carries no moment (Appendix J). The continuum Kubo responses below T∗T^{*} (Sec. IX.2) use λ=0.075​t\lambda=0.075\,t, and the spectrum shown in Sec. IX.2 uses λ=0.12​t\lambda=0.12\,t.

VI Linear-order Higgs–Yukawa sector and Z3000 node stability

The gauge-adjoint bilinear space consists of 28 multiplets: the 10 SO(5)-adjoint scalars Tr⁡[σa​𝒳¯​Tj​𝒳]\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\,T^{j}\mathcal{X}], the 15 SO(5)-vector currents Tr⁡[σa​𝒳¯​Γj​γμ​𝒳]\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\,\Gamma^{j}\gamma^{\mu}\mathcal{X}], and the 3 gauge currents Tr⁡[σa​𝒳¯​γμ​𝒳]\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\gamma^{\mu}\mathcal{X}]. We classify the Yukawa couplings Φsa​ℬa\Phi^{a}_{s}\,\mathcal{B}^{a} under the locked groups, with the Higgs representations fixed by the invariance of the Lagrangian of Sec. III. Without DM the classification returns the two zeroth-order Yukawa structures of Ref. [27]. With DM, D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} admits no new Yukawa coupling, and the in-plane components admit three new channels,

Φ1a​Tr​[σa​𝒳¯​μy​σx​γ0​𝒳]−Φ2a​Tr​[σa​𝒳¯​μy​σy​γ0​𝒳],\displaystyle\Phi_{1}^{a}\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mu^{y}\sigma^{x}\gamma^{0}\mathcal{X}]-\Phi_{2}^{a}\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mu^{y}\sigma^{y}\gamma^{0}\mathcal{X}],
Φ1a​Tr​[σa​𝒳¯​𝒳​σy]−Φ2a​Tr​[σa​𝒳¯​𝒳​σx],\displaystyle\Phi_{1}^{a}\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mathcal{X}\sigma^{y}]-\Phi_{2}^{a}\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mathcal{X}\sigma^{x}], (10)
Φ3a​Tr​[σa​𝒳¯​μy​(σx​γy+σy​γx)​𝒳],\displaystyle\Phi_{3}^{a}\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mu^{y}(\sigma^{x}\gamma^{y}+\sigma^{y}\gamma^{x})\mathcal{X}],

the last being the first zeroth-order Φ3\Phi_{3} coupling of the theory. At the multicritical point Φ1,2\Phi_{1,2} are critical and Φ3\Phi_{3} is not, so the first two channels are relevant there, and their size decides whether they matter. The γ0\gamma^{0} channel is an SO(5) and Lorentz partner of the SO(5)-breaking Yukawa coupling yy of Ref. [27], whose flavor matrices μz​γx\mu^{z}\gamma^{x}, μx​γy\mu^{x}\gamma^{y} lie in the same SO(5) vector and Lorentz vector, so at the SO(5) point it has the same scaling dimension. The scalar channel differs from yy only in the Dirac structure of the vertex; at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) only the gauge exchange between the two fermion legs distinguishes the two, and it makes the scalar channel less relevant than yy by 64/(3​π2​N)≃0.1864/(3\pi^{2}N)\simeq 0.18 at N=12N=12. Reference [27] obtains this difference for Yukawa vertices with and without Dirac structure [its Eq. (100)], in agreement with Appendix I. The bare sizes follow from the lattice. Deforming the π\pi-flux state along the Z3000 amplitudes and projecting the hopping and the Wick-decoupled DM operator on the nodes yields the Yukawa coupling y∝Δd+Δd′+2​Δg,1y\propto\Delta_{d}+\Delta_{d^{\prime}}+2\Delta_{g,1} of Ref. [27] and shows that only the intra-dimer DD generates the first two channels; the in-plane inter-dimer couplings feed only the Φ3\Phi_{3} channel, and D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} none. Each channel starts at 0.0060.006–0.0540.054 of yy per unit D/tD/t for the individual Z3000 amplitudes Δd,Δd′,Δg,1\Delta_{d},\Delta_{d^{\prime}},\Delta_{g,1} (Appendix I) and at 0.0330.033 for representative ones, i.e. at a ratio r≃6×10−4r\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}–2×10−22\times 10^{-2} for D/t≃0.1D/t\simeq 0.1–0.30.3. These ratios refer to a fixed direction of the Higgs field in amplitude space and do not bound the DM channels if yy is small through a cancellation among the Z3000 amplitudes. Barring such a cancellation, the γ0\gamma^{0} channel stays a factor rr below yy at every scale and the scalar channel falls further behind, so the pseudocritical window is terminated by yy itself and the DM-induced Yukawa couplings remain subleading within it. The conclusion does not rest on the sign of the O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) difference (Appendix I). In the Z3000 phase the DM-induced Yukawa couplings become quadratic terms ∝D​⟨Φ⟩\propto D\,\langle\Phi\rangle in the spinon Hamiltonian, and the absence of gauge-singlet masses does not decide whether they gap the Z3000 nodes. Diagonalization of the Bloch-resolved Z3000 Bogoliubov Hamiltonian together with the Wick-induced DM operator, with the nodes located by continuous minimization, shows that they remain gapless for each of the four DM components up to couplings far exceeding the material values, and also with all four components applied simultaneously in ranges of ratios of relevance to the material.

Analytically, the protection follows from a chiral symmetry. The full spinon Bogoliubov Hamiltonian including every DM coupling anticommutes with the unique staggered chiral operator 𝒮=(−1)ix+iy​𝒞M\mathcal{S}=(-1)^{i_{x}+i_{y}}\,\mathcal{C}_{M}, where 𝒞M\mathcal{C}_{M} is the on-site Majorana-component rotation. The staggered sign maps onto ρy​μy\rho^{y}\mu^{y} in the continuum, and 𝒮\mathcal{S} is the product of time reversal and particle–hole conjugation, so the protection is a symmetry statement. Each node therefore carries a chiral winding number and can disappear only by pairwise annihilation. The intra-dimer DD shifts the nodes along the zone diagonal. The in-plane inter-dimer components move them off the diagonal. In momenta conjugate to the translations by 2​a2a (aa the lattice spacing) of the 2×22\times 2 cell, each node splits into a pair displaced by ±(δkx,δky)≃±(0.067,−0.070)D∥,s′/t\pm(\delta k_{x},\delta k_{y})\simeq\pm(0.067,-0.070)\,D^{\prime}_{\parallel,s}/t (|δk|≃0.097D′∥,s/t|\delta k|\simeq 0.097\,D^{\prime}_{\parallel,s}/t) for the staggered component and by ±(0.059,−0.059)D∥,ns′/t\pm(0.059,-0.059)\,D^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns}/t for the non-staggered one, with slopes evaluated at the reference Z3000 ansatz. Qualitatively this displacement is the momentum-space counterpart of the ±4​λ\pm 4\lambda splitting of Sec. IX.2. D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} leaves the nodes in place at linear order.

VII Fate of D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}: flavored spin-2 currents at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N)

The physical operator OBO_{B} of Eq. (8) renormalizes as the flavor non-singlet spin-2 current OTμ​ν=Tr⁡[𝒳¯​ΓT​γ(μCLOSE​i​D↔​𝒳OPENν)]O_{T}^{\mu\nu}=\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\,\Gamma_{T}\gamma^{(\mu}\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}{}^{\nu)}\mathcal{X}], in ψ\psi form 2​ψ¯​μy​γ(μCLOSE​i​D↔​ψOPENν)2\bar{\psi}\mu^{y}\gamma^{(\mu}\mathrm{i}\overset{\leftrightarrow}{D}{}^{\nu)}\psi with Dμ=∂μ−iAaμσaD_{\mu}=\partial_{\mu}-\mathrm{i}A^{a}_{\mu}\sigma^{a}. Its flavor matrix ΓT=μy​σz\Gamma_{T}=\mu^{y}\sigma^{z} is a component of the SO(5) vector, and its QED3 analogue is the flavor-adjoint spin-2 current. The flavor matrix acts on valley and spin indices and commutes with the gauge generators. Being flavored, the operator cannot mix with gauge-field or Higgs operators at y=0y=0, and a single anomalous dimension governs it. We compute this dimension at leading order in 1/N1/N, with N=2​Nf+4​Nb=12N=2N_{f}+4N_{b}=12 the polarization count of Sec. III and Appendix H, using the diagrams of Fig. 2. The log-divergent integrals are collected in Appendix O. The same rules give the following results for related operators.

  1. 1.

    The flavored scalar bilinear, whose dimension ΔV\Delta_{V} governs the VBS channel of Secs. X and XII, acquires ΔV=2−64​Cg/(3​π2​N)=1.46\Delta_{V}=2-64C_{g}/(3\pi^{2}N)=1.46 at Cg=∑aσa​σa=3C_{g}=\sum_{a}\sigma^{a}\sigma^{a}=3, the Casimir factor of the SU(2) gauge vertex, independent of the gauge parameter. Reference [27] obtains the same dimension (its Eq. (79)), with the count N=2​Nf+4​NbN=2N_{f}+4N_{b} of Appendix H, which agrees with the rule of the companion U(1) analysis of Ref. [26] and is used throughout this paper.

  2. 2.

    The flavored conserved current has Δ=2\Delta=2 exactly, in every gauge and component.

  3. 3.

    With the gauge line replaced by a Gross–Neveu scalar (no seagull), the same rules give the published non-singlet spin-2 value γ2GN=16/(15​π2​n)\gamma_{2}^{\rm GN}=16/(15\pi^{2}n) for nn two-component flavors, i.e. 32/(15​π2​ncomp)32/(15\pi^{2}n_{\rm comp}) with ncomp=2​nn_{\rm comp}=2n components [Eq. (3.24) of Ref. [31] at d=3d=3, s=2s=2; Refs. [85, 75]] (Appendix O).

  4. 4.

    The result is independent of the external-momentum routing for the symmetric (two-sided) derivative vertex, with no admixture of other tensor structures.

The gauge-parameter dependence cancels between vertex and self-energy, and the seagull graphs are gauge-parameter free. The relative sign of the seagull and tree vertices is fixed by gauge covariance. With Dμ=∂μ−iAaμσaD_{\mu}=\partial_{\mu}-\mathrm{i}A^{a}_{\mu}\sigma^{a} the operator OTμ​νO_{T}^{\mu\nu} has tree vertex −μy​γ(μCLOSE​kOPENν)-\mu^{y}\gamma^{(\mu}k^{\nu)} and seagull vertex +μy​γ(μCLOSE​δαOPENν)​σa+\mu^{y}\gamma^{(\mu}\delta^{\nu)}_{\alpha}\sigma^{a} in ψ\psi form, and each seagull graph then equals −16Cg/(3π2N)-16C_{g}/(3\pi^{2}N) times the tree vertex (Appendix O). The result contains no free parameter,

γ2adj=64​Cg5​π2​N=165​π2≃+0.324,\gamma_{2}^{\rm adj}=\frac{64\,C_{g}}{5\pi^{2}N}=\frac{16}{5\pi^{2}}\simeq+0.324, (11)

the last equality at Cg=3C_{g}=3, N=12N=12, so ΔOB=3.32\Delta_{O_{B}}=3.32 and the D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}-induced coupling is irrelevant at leading order in 1/N1/N. Independently of the expansion, a non-conserved spin-2 primary of a unitary conformal field theory (CFT) has Δ>3\Delta>3 strictly, equality holding only for a conserved current [80, 25], and OBO_{B} is not conserved at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N). Within the assumed CFT the operator is therefore irrelevant, and the value 3.32 is its leading-order dimension. Non-conservation is an O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) effect, since at N=∞N=\infty the operator is a conserved higher-spin current. In the walking scenario with complex fixed points unitarity bounds do not apply strictly [125, 137]. For y≠0y\neq 0, SO(5) is broken and OBO_{B} may mix with Higgs spin-2 bilinears of the same lattice quantum numbers. In this sense, within the assumed CFT at y=0y=0, the largest inter-dimer DM coupling of SrCu2(BO3)2 is inert at the critical point at linear order among the fermion bilinears. Beyond bilinears, D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} enters four-fermion operators at linear order, an SO(5) 𝟑𝟓\mathbf{35} Lorentz vector with Δ=4\Delta=4 and a 𝟓\mathbf{5} spin-2 part with Δ=3.91\Delta=3.91 at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) (Appendix K), both irrelevant. At second order it seeds the rank-2 SO(5) tensor of Sec. VIII.

At Cg=1C_{g}=1, Eq. (11) reproduces the QED3 flavor-adjoint spin-2 anomalous dimension of Zhou and He, Eq. (79) of Ref. [136] at spin ℓ=2\ell=2, obtained with the same two-component counting and photon normalization Π=N​|q|/16\Pi=N|q|/16, and the flow dδ/dℓ=−64δ/(5π2N)d\delta/d\ell=-64\delta/(5\pi^{2}N) of the flavored velocity anisotropy δ\delta of the QED3 Dirac spin liquid [Eq. (17) of Ref. [46]], a component of the same spin-2 current. Because the seagull sign is fixed a priori, this agreement is an independent test of Eq. (11), and fixing the seagull vertex by minimal coupling alone gives the same result. The non-abelian placement of CgC_{g} follows Gracey’s general-dd, general-gauge-group result, Eq. (14) of Ref. [35], with Casimir structure C2​(R)/[T⁡(R)​Nf]C_{2}(R)/[T(R)N_{f}], whose master formula at d=3d=3 (his μ=3/2\mu=3/2) gives γ2=64/(5​π2​N)\gamma_{2}=64/(5\pi^{2}N) in two-component abelian conventions. The protected limits, the adjoint current at ℓ=1\ell=1 and the singlet spin-2 operator at ℓ=2\ell=2, have vanishing anomalous dimension, as they must [136]. The Chern–Simons-matter results of Ref. [12], for U(MM) Chern–Simons theory with NN fermion flavors, give vanishing O⁡(M/N)O(M/N) anomalous dimensions for the spin-1 and spin-2 singlet currents at every ’t Hooft coupling [its Eqs. (4.16), (4.17)]; at M=1M=1 and λM→∞\lambda_{M}\to\infty (QED3) its odd-spin result, Eq. (4.17), coincides with the tower below at Cg=1C_{g}=1. For reference, the full adjoint tower of spin-ℓ\ell currents in our theory reads

γℓadj=16​CgN​π2​[∑i=1ℓ1i−1/2−23​11​ℓ2−24​ℓ2−1],\gamma_{\ell}^{\rm adj}=\frac{16\,C_{g}}{N\pi^{2}}\Bigl[\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\frac{1}{i-1/2}-\frac{2}{3}\,\frac{11\ell^{2}-2}{4\ell^{2}-1}\Bigr], (12)

adapted from Ref. [136]. At Cg=3C_{g}=3 and N=12N=12 the prefactor is 4/π24/\pi^{2}, and ℓ=1\ell=1, 22 return 00 and Eq. (11), respectively. Continued to ℓ=0\ell=0, outside the range ℓ≥1\ell\geq 1 stated in Ref. [136], the formula returns ΔV−2\Delta_{V}-2, as does Eq. (14) of Ref. [35] at n=0n=0.

Perspective at O⁡(1/N2)O(1/N^{2}). No controlled next-order result exists for the mixed gauge–Higgs theory. The combination 64/(π2​N)64/(\pi^{2}N) that sets the scale of every one-loop anomalous dimension above equals 0.54 at N=12N=12, so the 1/N1/N results of this section are qualitative and fix only signs and orderings. The known analogues indicate the size and direction of the next order. The abelian QED3 adjoint dimension is 2−2.162/N−0.470/N22-2.162/N-0.470/N^{2} for NN two-component flavors [Ref. [33], Eq. (27); the leading term also in Ref. [3], Eq. (3.5)]. Its next-to-leading/leading (NLO/LO) ratio is 0.217/N≃1.8%0.217/N\simeq 1.8\% at N=12N=12. The non-abelian QCD3 analogue [16] carries a larger, CAC_{A}-dominated next-order term. For SU(2) its NLO/LO ratio is about 3.9/Nf3.9/N_{f} for NfN_{f} four-component flavors, so the abelian 1.8%1.8\% is not a size estimate for the present theory. Neither theory contains the adjoint-Higgs screening of the present one, whose O⁡(1/N2)O(1/N^{2}) contribution is uncomputed. Both known analogues shift ΔV\Delta_{V} further below 2, the direction that strengthens the conclusions drawn from it. We are not aware of an O⁡(1/N2)O(1/N^{2}) result for a flavored spin-2 current in any gauge theory. In the Gross–Neveu prototype the non-singlet spin-2 current at next order has the same sign as its leading term, γ2GN≃0.216/ncomp+0.645/ncomp2\gamma_{2}^{\rm GN}\simeq 0.216/n_{\rm comp}+0.645/n_{\rm comp}^{2} for ncompn_{\rm comp} fermion components [Ref. [75], Eqs. (3.5a) and (B.1)]. The O⁡(1/N2)O(1/N^{2}) computation for the present theory, whose new ingredient is the adjoint-Higgs polarization at criticality (Appendix H), is left to future work.

VIII DM-seeded SO(5) anisotropies

This section treats the DM-seeded perturbations at second order, which act above the crossover scale T∗=4​λT^{*}=4\lambda and below the length ξDM=v/(4​λ)\xi_{\rm DM}=v/(4\lambda) of Sec. IX.1, with vv the Dirac velocity. The mass-channel responses are computed in the λ\lambda-deformed spectrum, whose quadratic band touching (QBT) below T∗T^{*} and its gap channels are described in Sec. IX.2. At leading order in 1/N1/N the fermions are governed by the quadratic theory, so the mass-channel susceptibilities of the λ\lambda-deformed theory constitute the leading-order result, to all orders in λ\lambda. We compute all six mass-channel responses with the full static Kubo kernel at temperature TT,

ΠO=12​∑𝒌,i​jf⁡(Ei)−f⁡(Ej)Ej−Ei​|Oi​j|2,\Pi_{O}=\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{\bm{k},ij}\frac{f(E_{i})-f(E_{j})}{E_{j}-E_{i}}\,|O_{ij}|^{2}, (13)

with ff the Fermi function and EiE_{i} the band energies. The degenerate limit −f′​(E)-f^{\prime}(E) of the kernel supplies the intraband (Pauli) response. The Pauli term carries the intraband response of the Fermi pockets and is required for the pocket-forming Néelz channel. We quote δ​ΠO=ΠO​(λ)−ΠO​(0)\delta\Pi_{O}=\Pi_{O}(\lambda)-\Pi_{O}(0) in a continuum normalization defined by a momentum sum over the grid without the factor (2​π)−2(2\pi)^{-2} and with mass matrices of eigenvalues ±2\pm 2, so only signs and ratios are meaningful. The factor 12\tfrac{1}{2} removes the double counting of the Majorana basis. At λ=0\lambda=0 all six responses coincide. The locked symmetry allows three rank-2 tensors on the SO(5) vector: the two diagonal ones below and an off-diagonal one proportional to Vx​VyV_{x}V_{y}. The valley-blind identity of the quadratic theory, in which the Hamiltonian h⁡(𝒌)h(\bm{k}) of Sec. IX.2 contains no μ\mu matrices, forces the third coefficient to vanish at this order, which symmetry alone does not. Within the SO(5) vector the splitting decomposes into a singlet shift and the two diagonal tensors,

δ​Π|rank-2\displaystyle\delta\Pi\big|_{\text{rank-2}} =τ1​diag​(3,3,−2,−2,−2)\displaystyle=\tau_{1}\,\mathrm{diag}(3,3,-2,-2,-2)
+τ2​diag​(0,0,1,1,−2),\displaystyle\quad+\tau_{2}\,\mathrm{diag}(0,0,1,1,-2), (14)

in the channel order (Vx,Vy,Nx,Ny,Nz)(V_{x},V_{y},N_{x},N_{y},N_{z}) and in the normalization above.

The regime relevant for the pseudocritical theory is T≫4​λT\gg 4\lambda, where the responses are of order λ2\lambda^{2}. This regime is evaluated at λ=0.005​t\lambda=0.005\,t for T/λ=5T/\lambda=5–100100, with circular and square cutoffs between 1.21.2 and 2.42.4; the λ2\lambda^{2} scaling is confirmed at λ=0.0025​t\lambda=0.0025\,t. For T/λ≤20T/\lambda\leq 20 the Néel responses are δ​ΠNx,y=−β\delta\Pi_{N_{x,y}}=-\beta and δ​ΠNz≃−2​β\delta\Pi_{N_{z}}\simeq-2\beta, with T​β/λ2=184T\beta/\lambda^{2}=184–196196 independent of the cutoff. The gap channels show no universal term of this form, and their small remainder changes by a factor of up to six with the cutoff. Hence, τ1=4​β/15>0\tau_{1}=4\beta/15>0 and τ2=β/3>0\tau_{2}=\beta/3>0, with τ1/τ2=0.80\tau_{1}/\tau_{2}=0.80, and the signs of both tensors are the same as in the QBT regime below T∗T^{*} (Sec. IX.2). In the critical regime they come from a suppression of the Néel channels, and the singlet channels carry no universal term. The cutoff-independent content is therefore a Néel→\toVBS splitter and an easy-plane splitter of definite sign, both of order λ2/T\lambda^{2}/T. Both DM-seeded tensors are traceless and lie in the rank-2 symmetric traceless representation of SO(5), the 𝟏𝟒\mathbf{14}. Whether they matter depends on the dimension of that operator, on which the two descriptions of the SO(5) point disagree. In the large-NN theory of this paper the 𝟏𝟒\mathbf{14} has Δ=3.46\Delta=3.46 at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) (the rank-2 four-fermion tensor of Appendix K) and is irrelevant, so the SO(5)-breaking four-fermion scalar generated by DM at second order does not destabilize the fixed point above T∗T^{*} at this order. Every other SO(5)-breaking eigenvalue of the O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) four-fermion spectrum also exceeds 33, but in the representations 𝟓\mathbf{5} and 𝟏𝟎\mathbf{10} mixing with gauge and Higgs composites is not computed, so we make no statement at higher order in DM. The DM-induced Yukawa couplings of Sec. VI stay below the Yukawa coupling that bounds the pseudocritical window. For the SO(5) nonlinear sigma model with a Wess–Zumino–Witten term, the fuzzy-sphere study of Ref. [137] instead finds this operator relevant, with Δ𝟏𝟒=1.456​(12)<3\Delta_{\mathbf{14}}=1.456(12)<3, a value obtained in the walking region off the critical point; its authors identify the SO(3)×\timesSO(2)-invariant component, the τ1\tau_{1} tensor of Eq. (14), as the tuning operator of the Néel–VBS transition. If that relevance carries over to the pseudocritical regime, the O⁡(λ2)O(\lambda^{2}) tensors are not the leading DM-seeded ones. The out-of-plane coupling, whose mean-field image is the irrelevant bilinear OBO_{B}, generates the same tensor at second order, because OBO_{B} carries the Néelz flavor μy​σz\mu^{y}\sigma^{z} and the product OB×OBO_{B}\times O_{B} contains the 𝟏𝟒\mathbf{14}. The same Kubo kernel evaluated with the Wick-decoupled D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} operator gives, per (D⟂′/t)2(D^{\prime}_{\perp}/t)^{2} and in the normalization of Eq. (14), τ1=−0.18\tau_{1}=-0.18 and τ2=−1.94\tau_{2}=-1.94, nearly independent of temperature, quadratic (to numerical precision), and ultraviolet dominated (the continuum OBO_{B} model gives τ2=−(3/2​π)​Λeff​(D⟂′/t)2\tau_{2}=-(3/2\pi)\Lambda_{\rm eff}(D^{\prime}_{\perp}/t)^{2} with an effective cutoff Λeff≃4\Lambda_{\rm eff}\simeq 4). The D⟂′2D^{\prime 2}_{\perp} tensor is easy-axis, opposite to the easy-plane λ2\lambda^{2} tensor, and the ratio of the two is −0.030​(T/t)​(D⟂′/λ)2-0.030\,(T/t)(D^{\prime}_{\perp}/\lambda)^{2}. For D⟂′=0.10D^{\prime}_{\perp}=0.10–0.180.18 meV and the Fock values λ=0.008\lambda=0.008–0.0250.025 K the D⟂′2D^{\prime 2}_{\perp} tensor is therefore comparable to the λ2\lambda^{2} one at T∗T^{*} and dominates above T×≃0.01T_{\times}\simeq 0.01–0.30.3 K. With yT=3−Δ𝟏𝟒≃1.54y_{T}=3-\Delta_{\mathbf{14}}\simeq 1.54 a coupling gTg_{T} of the 𝟏𝟒\mathbf{14} becomes of order one at ET=Λ​gT1/yTE_{T}=\Lambda g_{T}^{1/y_{T}}, with Λ≃t\Lambda\simeq t unless stated. The mean-field coefficient, gT≃0.014​(D⟂′/t)2g_{T}\simeq 0.014(D^{\prime}_{\perp}/t)^{2}, gives ET≃0.03E_{T}\simeq 0.03–0.070.07 K, of order T∗T^{*}; a bond-level XXZ estimate, D⟂′2/2​J′2≃0.08​(D⟂′/t)2D^{\prime 2}_{\perp}/2J^{\prime 2}\simeq 0.08(D^{\prime}_{\perp}/t)^{2}, gives 0.10.1–0.20.2 K (0.20.2–0.50.5 K with Λ=J′\Lambda=J^{\prime}), and a coefficient of order one would give 0.50.5–11 K. These estimates concern the magnitude only. The bond-level XXZ anisotropy is easy-plane, whereas the easy-axis sign found above is a free-spinon mean-field result dominated by lattice-scale momenta, so the sign of the D⟂′2D^{\prime 2}_{\perp} tensor is not a universal statement. The intra-dimer DD has no mean-field image on the π\pi-flux state, since its Wick amplitude vanishes on the dimer bonds, so its O⁡(D2)O(D^{2}) tensor, like the symmetric intra-dimer anisotropies Jz​zJ_{zz} and Jx​yJ_{xy} of the neutron fit of Ref. [79] and the dipolar coupling, which are of the same order, lies outside this theory. The symmetric anisotropy cannot be dropped against the second-order DM effects: for a single bond, DM and the symmetric anisotropy of the same order are equivalent to isotropic exchange by a local spin rotation, and only their frustration across bonds has observable consequences [104].

If the 𝟏𝟒\mathbf{14} is relevant, the DM-seeded SO(5) breaking above T∗T^{*} is a second-order anisotropy, easy-axis at mean field (a sign that is not universal, see above) and, with τ1<0\tau_{1}<0, tilted toward the Néel side. It acts at a scale of order T∗T^{*} or above, up to about 11 K, and the statement that DM cannot destabilize the pseudocritical regime above T∗T^{*} then holds at linear order only. The same second-order seed also carries an SO(5)-singlet component, −2.1-2.1 per (D⟂′/t)2(D^{\prime}_{\perp}/t)^{2}, which shifts the tuning parameter but breaks no symmetry. Beyond ξDM\xi_{\rm DM} the competition among these channels is decided by the QBT flow of Sec. X.1. Within the λ2\lambda^{2} tensors alone the deconfined Néel–VBS competition is tilted toward the singlet side and residual magnetism is easy-plane, statements that hold below T×T_{\times}. The signs of τ1\tau_{1} and τ2\tau_{2} are leading-order statements (Sec. VII).

IX Crossover scale and the band touching

IX.1 RG eigenvalue and scales

𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM} is built from the Noether currents of the spin SU(2) symmetry, which is conserved at the lattice level in the unperturbed model. Its scaling dimension is therefore exactly 2 at any genuine fixed point of the unperturbed theory, and λ\lambda has RG eigenvalue +1+1 with no anomalous correction at any order. In the pseudocritical (walking) regime of Ref. [27], the flow stays close to the SO(5)-symmetric fixed point, expected to be conformal at vanishing Yukawa coupling, until the Yukawa coupling yy drives it away. That coupling is relevant in the large-flavor expansion of Ref. [27], with RG eigenvalue ≃1.38\simeq 1.38 at Nf=Nb=2N_{f}=N_{b}=2, and its authors regard the fate of yy at these values as unclear. A window reaching down to T∗T^{*} requires a correspondingly small bare value of yy, which grows by a factor of 3×1033\times 10^{3}–3×1043\times 10^{4} between J′J^{\prime} and T∗T^{*}. In this regime the RG eigenvalue of λ\lambda is 1 up to corrections controlled by the flow of the Yukawa coupling. The same holds, with corrections controlled by the slow drift of the couplings, in the pseudocritical scenario of Ref. [125], where the flow passes near a pair of complex fixed points and no fixed point is reached at real couplings. Hence

ξDM≃v4​λ,T∗≃4​λ=2​χ0​|DΣ′|≃0.34​|DΣ′|.\xi_{\rm DM}\simeq\frac{v}{4\lambda},\qquad T^{*}\simeq 4\lambda=\sqrt{2}\,\chi_{0}\,|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|\simeq 0.34\,|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|. (15)

The eigenvalue is exact at a fixed point. The prefactor of λ\lambda carries the O⁡(1)O(1) uncertainty of the mean-field matching of Sec. V.3.

DΣ′D^{\prime}_{\Sigma} is not the triplon combination D~∥\tilde{D}_{\parallel} constrained by dimer-phase spectroscopy [14, 94], and its value rests on the DFT vectors of Ref. [77] (Sec. II): DΣ′≃−0.014D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}\simeq-0.014 meV, or |DΣ′|≃0.007|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|\simeq 0.007–0.0250.025 meV with the tabulated precision and an ESR rescaling. At the Fock level this gives T∗≃0.03T^{*}\simeq 0.03–0.10.1 K. The value of Sec. V.3 is the Fock one: at linear order in DD the DM term is a background spin gauge field, a twist of the Fock hopping χ0​J′\chi_{0}J^{\prime} by the angle Dbond′/J′D^{\prime}_{\rm bond}/J^{\prime}, so the node splitting scales with the spinon velocity, 4​λ=2​(t/J′)​|DΣ′|4\lambda=\sqrt{2}\,(t/J^{\prime})\,|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}| for a hopping tt, and it is the length ξDM=v/(4​λ)=2​(J′/|DΣ′|)​a\xi_{\rm DM}=v/(4\lambda)=\sqrt{2}\,(J^{\prime}/|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|)\,a that does not depend on tt. We take the π\pi-flux Dirac velocity v=2​t​av=2ta, aa the square-lattice spacing, and assume t≃0.4​J′t\simeq 0.4J^{\prime}, a value not derived here and 1.71.7 times the Fock value χ0​J′≃0.24​J′\chi_{0}J^{\prime}\simeq 0.24J^{\prime}. With it the same twist gives T∗≃0.57​|DΣ′|≃0.05T^{*}\simeq 0.57|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|\simeq 0.05–0.170.17 K. We therefore quote T∗≃0.03T^{*}\simeq 0.03–0.10.1 K at the Fock level, up to 0.170.17 K with t≃0.4​J′t\simeq 0.4J^{\prime}. The range T∗≃0.03T^{*}\simeq 0.03–0.170.17 K used elsewhere in this paper includes the tabulated precision, the ESR rescaling and this prefactor. For J′=51J^{\prime}=51–5454 K this gives t≃20t\simeq 20–2222 K and ξDM≃250\xi_{\rm DM}\simeq 250–470470 lattice spacings (940940 at |DΣ′|=0.007|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|=0.007 meV).

The energy 4​λ4\lambda is the scale of the node reconstruction. The thermodynamic crossover lies an order of magnitude lower, because the reconstructed band v2​k2+4​λ2−2​λ\sqrt{v^{2}k^{2}+4\lambda^{2}}-2\lambda is quadratic only for energies well below λ\lambda. For free spinons the specific heat of h⁡(𝒌)h(\bm{k}) of Sec. IX.2 stays within 5%5\% of its Dirac value down to T≃0.15×4​λT\simeq 0.15\times 4\lambda. Its local exponent d​ln⁡C/d​ln⁡Td\ln C/d\ln T is 1.421.42 at 0.1×4​λ0.1\times 4\lambda and 1.121.12 at 0.02×4​λ0.02\times 4\lambda. For the material the thermodynamic crossover is therefore at about 33–2525 mK, and C∝TC\propto T is approached only near 0.02​T∗0.02\,T^{*}, i.e. 0.60.6–33 mK, comparable to the instability scale T∗⁣∗T^{**} of Sec. X.1. Above T∗T^{*} the Dirac spin liquid and the SO(5) pseudocritical window are protected against the DM perturbation at linear order by the RG eigenvalue 1 and the small prefactor; the second-order anisotropies were treated in Sec. VIII. This range covers nearly all temperatures explored experimentally in SrCu2(BO3)2. The lowest NMR temperature under pressure, 0.070.07 K [20], lies near T∗T^{*}.

The twist structure of 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM} parallels, but does not reproduce, the reducible/irreducible classification of Cheng et al. [14]. There the non-staggered in-plane component, after a uniform dimer rotation, sums to zero around closed loops and is removed to first order, whereas D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} and D~∥\tilde{D}_{\parallel} are not. In the Dirac theory, at strictly linear order, the coupling λ​𝒪DM\lambda\,\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM}, which contains D′∥,sD^{\prime}_{\parallel,s} and D′∥,nsD^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns} with equal weight, is twist-equivalent to spin-dependent node displacements. No rotation removes the ±4​λ\pm 4\lambda splitting into the quadratic band touching or the O⁡(λ2)O(\lambda^{2}) anisotropies of Sec. VIII. The obstruction to removing them is non-abelian, [Axspin,Ayspin]≠0[A^{\rm spin}_{x},A^{\rm spin}_{y}]\neq 0, and differs from the loop-sum criterion of Ref. [14].

IX.2 Quadratic band touching below T∗T^{*}

Diagonalizing h⁡(𝒌)=v⁡(kx​ρx−ky​ρz)+λ​hDMh(\bm{k})=v(k_{x}\rho^{x}-k_{y}\rho^{z})+\lambda h_{\rm DM} at Γ\Gamma splits the eightfold multiplet into branches at ±4​λ\pm 4\lambda and four gapless modes (Fig. 3). Second-order k⋅pk\!\cdot\!p theory gives the canonical dd-wave quadratic band touching

HQBT​(𝒌)=v24​λ​[(kx2−ky2)​𝒜1+2​kx​ky​𝒜2],{𝒜1,𝒜2}=0,H_{\rm QBT}(\bm{k})=\frac{v^{2}}{4\lambda}\bigl[(k_{x}^{2}-k_{y}^{2})\,\mathcal{A}_{1}+2k_{x}k_{y}\,\mathcal{A}_{2}\bigr],\ \ \{\mathcal{A}_{1},\mathcal{A}_{2}\}=0, (16)

with no k2​ 1k^{2}\,\mathds{1} term. Such a term is forbidden by the chiral symmetry 𝒞=ρy\mathcal{C}=\rho^{y}, which anticommutes with the full h⁡(𝒌)h(\bm{k}) including the DM term and acts within the band-touching subspace. The Berry winding is 2, and the spectrum is isotropic at all kk, with no cubic warping. The spinon density of states is finite at energies well below λ\lambda, giving C∼TC\sim T in the free-spinon regime for T≪0.1×4​λT\ll 0.1\times 4\lambda (Sec. IX.1). Since T∗⁣∗≃(0.008CLOSET^{**}\simeq(0.008–OPEN0.025)×4​λ0.025)\times 4\lambda (Sec. X.1), this regime spans at most a factor of a few in temperature before the instability. We do not infer a constant spin susceptibility or a finite intrinsic κ0/T\kappa_{0}/T from this. The projected uniform-zz spin equals minus the flux mass and shares the gap-channel infrared logarithm, and a clean quadratic band supplies no momentum-relaxation mechanism. Transport requires disorder or gauge scattering and is not computed here.

Mass content of the QBT. Projecting the six masses onto the QBT subspace gives the following. Néelx,y vanish identically, since they live entirely on the ±4​λ\pm 4\lambda branches. VBSx, VBSy, and the flux (scalar-chirality) mass anticommute with both 𝒜1,2\mathcal{A}_{1,2} and open full gaps. Néelz survives with equal norm but commutes with 𝒜1,2\mathcal{A}_{1,2}, so it splits the bands into Fermi pockets without opening a gap, and a zero-energy ring persists in its spectrum. The QBT therefore has three gauge-singlet gap channels, and Néel (staggered-magnetic) gapping is excluded kinematically. On the QBT subspace the projected uniform spin density obeys P⁡(J0​σz)=−P⁡(flux)P(J^{0}\sigma^{z})=-P(\text{flux}) exactly, so the flux gap coincides there with the uniform-zz magnetization channel. Chirality and uniform zz magnetization are locked, so a chiral gap carries weak zz ferromagnetism, and a field 𝑩|[001]\bm{B}\parallel[001] couples linearly to the flux channel. The [001][001] entry of the field classification of Sec. XI follows independently from this identity.

Mass-channel responses below T∗T^{*}. With the Kubo kernel of Sec. VIII, Table 5 lists the responses at λ=0.075​t\lambda=0.075t on the grid |kx|,|ky|≤1.2|k_{x}|,|k_{y}|\leq 1.2 with 3602360^{2} points. With 4​λ=0.3​t4\lambda=0.3t, all tabulated temperatures lie below T∗T^{*}.

The three gap channels are equal at every TT. This equality is the kinematic identity of the valley-blind quadratic theory and is lifted only at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N). Their common value grows logarithmically as T→0T\to 0 (the gap-channel infrared logarithm, regulated here by TT), and it crosses zero near T∼0.1​tT\sim 0.1t at a cutoff-dependent position. The individual δ​ΠO\delta\Pi_{O} are matching-dependent and carry no invariant sign. The Néel channels saturate. At low TT the Néelz response is the sum of an interband depression (−27.4-27.4) and the pocket Pauli term (+7.4+7.4). In the decomposition of Eq. (14), τ1​(T)>0\tau_{1}(T)>0 grows logarithmically, to 8.178.17 at T=0.0016​tT=0.0016t, and τ2=+1.953\tau_{2}=+1.953 (|ki|≤1.2|k_{i}|\leq 1.2) or +2.092+2.092 (|ki|≤1.6|k_{i}|\leq 1.6) saturates below T≃0.02​tT\simeq 0.02t and must be quoted with its ultraviolet prescription. The logarithmic growth of τ1\tau_{1}, the positive gap-channel response and its zero crossing are properties of the QBT regime.

X Instabilities of the band touching

The regime below T∗T^{*} treated in Sec. IX.2 and in this section rests on five conditions, each stated where it arises and collected here. (i) A pseudocritical window that reaches T∗T^{*}, which requires a small bare Yukawa coupling (Sec. IX.1), and the second-order anisotropies must not act first, which they may if the 𝟏𝟒\mathbf{14} is relevant (Sec. VIII). (ii) Proximity to the critical pressure. The band touching exists between the Higgs splitting δ′\delta^{\prime} of Eq. (18) and λ\lambda, a window open for Higgs-deviation scales sH≲0.03s_{H}\lesssim 0.03–0.080.08 at d=0.6d=0.6 and for smaller sHs_{H} at the material λ\lambda (Sec. X.3), and no measurement fixes sHs_{H}. (iii) A two-dimensional sample. The interlayer coupling Jc=0.053​(3)J_{c}=0.053(3) meV≃0.6{}\simeq 0.6 K, fitted at 5.55.5 GPa in the monoclinic phase [28] and assumed here to carry over to the tetragonal one, exceeds T∗T^{*} by a factor 44–2020 and T∗⁣∗T^{**} by two to three orders of magnitude. If JcJ_{c} couples the Néel vectors of adjacent layers, through 𝑵1⋅𝑵2\bm{N}_{1}\cdot\bm{N}_{2} of dimension 2​ΔN2\Delta_{N}, with ΔN\Delta_{N} the scaling dimension of the Néel order parameter, the dimensional crossover lies near J′​(Jc/J′)1/(3−2​ΔN)J^{\prime}(J_{c}/J^{\prime})^{1/(3-2\Delta_{N})}, negligible at the leading-order ΔN=1.46\Delta_{N}=1.46 and about 44 K at ΔN≃0.63\Delta_{N}\simeq 0.63. (iv) Clean samples. The random valence-bond field of point defects becomes strong near 0.10.1–0.30.3 K for free-spin fractions of 0.10.1–0.4%0.4\%, comparable to T∗T^{*} (Sec. XII). (v) No order above T∗T^{*}. The samples measured so far order above 11 K. Within these conditions the instability scale is T∗⁣∗≃(0.03CLOSET^{**}\simeq(0.03–OPEN0.1)​λ0.1)\lambda, 0.20.2–2.52.5 mK at the Fock level (up to 44 mK with t≃0.4​J′t\simeq 0.4J^{\prime}), an order-of-magnitude one-loop estimate, and the basin fractions found below depend on the sampling measure of the initial couplings.

X.1 Infrared fate: interactions at the QBT

In the Higgsed (Z3000) phase the SU(2) gauge field acquires a Higgs mass mAm_{A}, proportional to the Higgs amplitude and vanishing at the critical point, and below mAm_{A} the gauge sector is gapped to ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2}. The band touching exists between the Higgs-induced splitting δ′\delta^{\prime} of Eq. (18) and the upper end of its quadratic regime, an energy of order λ\lambda (Sec. IX.1). Near the critical point, where the window is open, mAm_{A} lies below λ\lambda over most of this range, and between mAm_{A} and λ\lambda the QBT couples to the unscreened SU(2) gauge field. The band touching screens this field itself (Appendix L). Its finite density of states gives the color density of the eight QBT modes the static polarization Π00=4​ln⁡2​ρ0\Pi_{00}=4\ln 2\,\rho_{0}, which removes the long-range color-Coulomb field. The transverse field couples through the velocity vertex, and its effective strength falls as (E/λ)1/2(E/\lambda)^{1/2}. The Higgs polarization, of relative size 1.1​(E/λ)1/21.1(E/\lambda)^{1/2} at the momenta of the window, is smaller than Π00\Pi_{00} well below λ\lambda, and so is the Higgs-mass term as long as mA≲λm_{A}\lesssim\lambda. On both sides of mAm_{A} the gauge field therefore leaves a short-range interaction U2​∑aρa​ρa\tfrac{U}{2}\sum_{a}\rho^{a}\rho^{a} between the color densities ρa\rho^{a}, with the strength ρ0​U=1/(4​ln⁡2)≃0.36\rho_{0}U=1/(4\ln 2)\simeq 0.36 at low energy, where ρ0=λ/(π​v2)\rho_{0}=\lambda/(\pi v^{2}) is the single-band density of states. The problem then falls in the marginally relevant QBT class of Refs. [114, 119]. On a single spinless QBT a weak repulsion VV grows as d​V/d​ℓ=ρ0​V2dV/d\ell=\rho_{0}V^{2} [114], with ℓ\ell the logarithm of the momentum cutoff. With several channels a pure density coupling has no one-loop term of its own but generates the others, which run away [119]. Here, the color interaction, which couples the fourteen channels, grows faster (Appendix L). It drives an instability into one of the gap channels analyzed below at T∗⁣∗∼E2​e−2​ℓ∗T^{**}\sim E_{2}\,e^{-2\ell^{*}}, with E2E_{2} the upper end of the short-range regime and ℓ∗\ell^{*} the flow time at which the couplings diverge. Néel gapping is excluded kinematically (Sec. IX.2). The three channels are degenerate at quadratic level by valley-blindness, but gauge fluctuations lift the degeneracy at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N). The flux mass is a flavor singlet and receives the two-photon annihilation (closed-loop) correction shown in Fig. 2(e),(f), familiar from the QED3 singlet [47, 15, 3], whereas the VBS (valley-adjoint) and Néel loops are traceless. In our theory this class is evaluated in Appendix O. The topology weight |Ctopo|=1/2|C_{\rm topo}|=1/2 follows from the 48 labeled contractions of the annihilation topology and the routing sign from momentum conservation on the fermion line, and together they give the QED3 value Δsinglet−Δadj=+64/(π2N)\Delta_{\rm singlet}-\Delta_{\rm adj}=+64/(\pi^{2}N) for NN two-component fermions. In the present theory the flavor loop carries tr⁡(σa​σb)=2​δa​b{\rm tr}(\sigma^{a}\sigma^{b})=2\delta^{ab} per valley, summed over the NfN_{f} valleys, the fermion line carries ∑aσa​σa=Cg=3\sum_{a}\sigma^{a}\sigma^{a}=C_{g}=3, and the two gauge propagators carry (16/N)2(16/N)^{2} with N=2​Nf+4​Nb=12N=2N_{f}+4N_{b}=12 (Sec. III). The result is

Δflux−ΔVBS=64π2​6​NfN2=163​π2≃+0.54,\Delta_{\rm flux}-\Delta_{\rm VBS}=\frac{64}{\pi^{2}}\,\frac{6N_{f}}{N^{2}}=\frac{16}{3\pi^{2}}\simeq+0.54, (17)

so ΔVBS≃1.46\Delta_{\rm VBS}\simeq 1.46 and Δflux=2+O⁡(1/N2)\Delta_{\rm flux}=2+O(1/N^{2}). The O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) correction to the latter cancels accidentally, since 6​Nf⋅64/(π2​N2)=64​Cg/(3​π2​N)6N_{f}\cdot 64/(\pi^{2}N^{2})=64C_{g}/(3\pi^{2}N) holds for Nb=NfN_{b}=N_{f}. The chirality channel is suppressed relative to VBS as T∗T^{*} is approached from above.

The Fierz-complete one-loop flow in this symmetry class (Appendix E) settles the competition. The locked group admits 14 invariant quartic couplings of the eight QBT Majorana modes, and with the analytic z=2z{=}2 bubble the β\beta function closes on this space. On a single spinless QBT it gives the marginal relevance of repulsion and the dominance of the time-reversal-breaking gap channel found in Ref. [114]. The pocket-splitting Néelz channel has identically vanishing gap-channel rate in every flow, as the kinematic exclusion requires. The flow has two stable runaway rays: a VBS-symmetric ray with equal VBSx/VBSy vertex growth and suppressed chirality, and a chirality ray with dominant flux vertex growth and suppressed VBS. Attraction in either gap channel selects its own ray, repulsion in one funnels into the other, and Néelz-type seeds of either sign flow to VBS. We scan random initial couplings, uniform on the Frobenius sphere, as a proxy measure for the unknown microscopic couplings. This measure is canonical for orthonormal Majorana modes but carries no microscopic information. Labeled by the fastest-growing channel when the couplings first reach |g|=200|g|=200, 487487 of 600600 seeds (81%±1.6%81\%\pm 1.6\%) are VBS, 111111 are flux, and two do not diverge up to the integration cutoff ℓ=60\ell=60 (in the physical normalization of Appendix E). On the asymptotic ray 8383–84%84\% are VBS, a value reproduced by a second sample of 600 seeds (Appendix E). Neither fraction is universal, since the ultraviolet matching and the sampling measure enter, but for this sampling the flux basin is clearly the smaller one. At the critical point only the six gauge-singlet quartics are legitimate (Appendix E). A census of 600 seeds drawn inside that subspace, which the flow preserves to 10−1510^{-15}, gives valence-bond order for 73%±2%73\%\pm 2\%, the flux mass for 25%25\% and no instability for 3%3\%, so the majority verdict holds there as well. On the majority ray the enhanced source sector is fivefold: the VBS pair together with the three gauge-adjoint μy\mu^{y}-flavored mass directions, with equal rates. The full local mass space of the eight modes is six-dimensional. The adjoint directions have no overlap with the six symmetry-allowed bilinears on the QBT modes discussed below, so they are symmetry-breaking order parameters. At the critical point they are not gauge-invariant, but in the Higgsed phase, where the flow applies, they become gauge-invariant once dressed by the condensate. On the ray itself the one-loop flow does not select among these five directions, so its majority terminus is VBS or adjoint-mass order unless the approach to the ray selects, as the gauge interaction below does in favor of VBS. The VBSx/VBSy rates on the ray are equal, and the selection within the doublet is discussed in Sec. X.3. The dimension splitting of Eq. (17) enhances the magnitude of the VBS quartic relative to the flux quartic at the matching scale but does not fix its sign. It favors the VBS terminus only if that quartic is attractive. At tree level the exchange of the material makes it attractive, g=J′g=J^{\prime}, and the flux channel repulsive (Sec. X.3), and the seed flows to the VBS ray. The O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) running between the lattice scale and λ\lambda keeps the signs of the VBS and Néelz channels and turns the flux channel attractive, and the running seed ends on the VBS ray for every value of the constraint-field dimension Δσ\Delta_{\sigma}, which is not controlled at N=12N=12 (Sec. X.3). In the static limit the screened gauge interaction is attractive with equal Hartree–Fock weight, +1.08+1.08 in the units of Appendix K, in the flux, VBS and Néelz channels, and repulsive in the gauge-adjoint masses, and it reaches the VBS ray at ℓ∗≃0.8\ell^{*}\simeq 0.8. Its full one-loop propagator contains the frequency dependence of the color polarization, the transverse field, screened only by the orbital response of the band touching and of the gapped Dirac background, and the polarization of the critical Higgs fields (Appendix L and Fig. 7(e),(f)). With it the gauge interaction projects onto a gauge-singlet seed whose overlap with the static one exceeds 0.99950.9995 below λ/4\lambda/4 and whose norm is 1.31.3–1.41.4 times the static one at 10−4​λ10^{-4}\lambda and 0.80.8 times at λ/4\lambda/4. Dynamical screening tilts it toward the chirality channel, and the transverse field tilts it back. The seed lies in the VBS basin at every scale of the window, in every scale-covariant gauge and momentum routing, and reaches the VBS ray at ℓ∗≃0.6\ell^{*}\simeq 0.6–1.11.1 at fixed scale. The margin stays small: across the window and the schemes a chirality-attractive admixture of about 22–4%4\% of its norm sends it to the chirality ray, against 2.62.6–3.1%3.1\% for the static seed. Higgs exchange through the SO(5)-breaking Yukawa coupling reaches the band touching only through the ±4​λ\pm 4\lambda states and is chirality-attractive. It moves the seed across the separatrix only if it is at least as strong as the gauge exchange at the scale λ\lambda, which requires the Yukawa coupling to have ended the pseudocritical window, and the DM-induced Yukawa channels change the margin by about 10−410^{-4}. On the way the static seed favors the VBS pair over the gauge-adjoint masses (rates 0.360.36 and 0.280.28 at |g|=200|g|=200), and the asymptotic ray restores their degeneracy. Added to the renormalized lattice seeds with any relative weight between 0.030.03 and 10310^{3}, it leaves both the VBS terminus and the sign of the plaquette selection of Sec. X.3 unchanged. Being valley-blind, it selects no plaquette pattern itself. The VBS verdict for the material therefore rests mainly on the VBS attraction of the exchange seed, which dominates after the running. The gauge interaction alone reaches the VBS ray only by a small margin. A repulsive VBS seed funnels into the chirality ray. The gapped chiral ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} spin liquid, with spontaneous scalar chirality, weak zz ferromagnetism by the chirality–magnetization locking above, and a quantized thermal Hall response (Sec. X.2), survives as a minority-basin alternative that requires chirality-attractive residual interactions that overcome the VBS attraction of the running exchange seed and the small VBS preference of the gauge interaction. Ordering through the Néelz pockets or through high-energy modes is a separate question not addressed by the mass projections. For a single spinless QBT, weak repulsion drives the time-reversal-breaking quantum anomalous Hall state [114]; with the many channels of the present band touching, the corresponding chiral outcome is instead the minority one for uniformly sampled couplings.

Protection, and the Higgsed-phase window. At the π\pi-flux/critical point the QBT is protected beyond the chiral argument: the unique locked-invariant gauge-singlet bilinear is 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM} itself, whose projection on the QBT subspace vanishes because the QBT is its null space. No symmetry-allowed bilinear exists there at all, so the vanishing one-loop tadpole is symmetry-required. In the Higgsed Z3000 phase the locked group admits six gauge-adjoint k0k^{0} bilinears on the QBT modes, two triplets such as the μy\mu^{y}-flavored analogue of 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM}. The condensates dress them into allowed couplings by the same mechanism as the zeroth-order Φ3\Phi_{3} Yukawa of Sec. VI. These split the touching without gapping it, and the nodes remain gapless throughout. On the lattice the splitting depends on the lattice DM amplitude dd and on the Higgs-deviation scale sHs_{H}, which multiplies the deviations of the Z3000 ansatz from the π\pi-flux state, δ​θ=0.30​sH\delta\theta=0.30\,s_{H} and (Δd,Δd′,Δg,1,Δg,2)=sH​(0.4,0.25,0.15,0.10)(\Delta_{d},\Delta_{d^{\prime}},\Delta_{g,1},\Delta_{g,2})=s_{H}(0.4,0.25,0.15,0.10) in units of tt. The splitting δ′≡min𝒌⁡E(3)​(𝒌)\delta^{\prime}\equiv\min_{\bm{k}}E_{(3)}(\bm{k}), with E(3)E_{(3)} the third-lowest excitation energy, vanishes identically at sH=0s_{H}=0 and obeys a second-order law,

δ′=(cΦ​sH​t)24​λ,cΦ≃0.67,\delta^{\prime}=\frac{(c_{\Phi}\,s_{H}\,t)^{2}}{4\lambda},\qquad c_{\Phi}\simeq 0.67, (18)

with δ′⋅4​λ\delta^{\prime}\cdot 4\lambda independent of dd to a few percent over a factor 44 in dd. It arises from virtual excursions through the ±4​λ\pm 4\lambda bands, quadratic in the Higgs deviation. The quartic flow thus runs over the energy window [δ′,λ][\delta^{\prime},\lambda], since the screened gauge interaction is present on both sides of mAm_{A} for mA≲λm_{A}\lesssim\lambda. For the screened gauge interaction alone ℓ∗≃0.8\ell^{*}\simeq 0.8 in the static limit and 0.60.6–1.11.1 with its full one-loop propagator at fixed scale (Appendix L). Followed scale by scale, with the Higgs polarization weakening the interaction toward the upper end of the window, ℓ∗≃0.9\ell^{*}\simeq 0.9–1.61.6 for E2E_{2} between λ/4\lambda/4 and 4​λ4\lambda. Random seeds of strength 0.50.5 in bubble units diverge at ℓ∗=4.6\ell^{*}=4.6–5252 (Appendix E), with median 10.810.8. At z=2z=2 an energy window [E1,E2][E_{1},E_{2}] corresponds to the flow time 12​ln⁡(E2/E1)\tfrac{1}{2}\ln(E_{2}/E_{1}). The quadratic regime ends at an energy E2E_{2} of order λ\lambda, so the basin verdict requires ln⁡[2​λ/(cΦ​sH​t)]≳ℓ∗\ln[2\lambda/(c_{\Phi}s_{H}t)]\gtrsim\ell^{*}, i.e. cΦ​sH​t≲0.5​λc_{\Phi}s_{H}t\lesssim 0.5\lambda, and the instability sets in at T∗⁣∗≃E2​e−2​ℓ∗T^{**}\simeq E_{2}e^{-2\ell^{*}}. This is (0.03CLOSE(0.03–OPEN0.1)​λ0.1)\lambda for E2E_{2} between λ/4\lambda/4 and λ\lambda, and up to 0.2​λ0.2\lambda if the flow is extended to E2=4​λE_{2}=4\lambda. Gauge fluctuations also flatten the band touching, raising the dynamical exponent to z≃2.2z\simeq 2.2 at low energy, which lowers these values by 55–15%15\%. They are order-of-magnitude estimates, since the couplings reach order one already at ℓ∗≲1\ell^{*}\lesssim 1, outside the range where a one-loop flow is controlled. The window opens logarithmically on approach to the critical point and closes deep in the Higgsed phase. At the reference Z3000 parameters with all four DM couplings the node disperses linearly down to the smallest resolved momenta. Where the window closes, the low-energy theory is a spin liquid with displaced, chirally protected linear Dirac nodes. Short-range quartic interactions are irrelevant there, and the stronger VBS tendency of Eq. (17), a property of the critical theory, does not by itself drive the system into an ordered phase. Possible strong-coupling instabilities of the deep-Z3000 Dirac phase require a separate analysis that we do not perform. The window criterion therefore bounds the regime of every T∗⁣∗T^{**} statement in this paper.

X.2 The chiral endpoint: lattice ansatz, Chern number, and thermal Hall response

The chiral outcome of the flow, in which the flux mass grows, can be realized as an explicit mean-field state on the lattice, whose Chern number and thermal Hall response we compute. On the lattice the flux mass is found by projecting every 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd spin-singlet amplitude in the Z3000 gauge onto the 36 continuum bilinears (Appendix J). The only gauge-singlet ones are imaginary singlet hoppings u0u^{0} on the diagonal bonds. Each of them projects onto the flux mass (±14\pm\tfrac{1}{4}) together with the 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd valley density Tr⁡[𝒳¯​γ0​μy​𝒳]\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\gamma^{0}\mu^{y}\mathcal{X}] (±14\pm\tfrac{1}{4}), and the latter cancels between the two diagonals of every square when they carry opposite signs. The pure flux mass is therefore the chiral pattern 𝒫χ\mathcal{P}_{\chi} of Eq. (41), with ∓u0\mp u^{0} on the dimer and orthogonal diagonals of the crossed squares and ±u0\pm u^{0} on the two diagonals of the empty squares.It projects onto the flux mass alone, with no admixture of the valley density. Under the Z3000 PSG it is translation-even, odd under GxG_{x}, σx​y\sigma_{xy} and 𝒯\mathcal{T}, and even under 𝒯​Gx\mathcal{T}G_{x} and 𝒯​σx​y\mathcal{T}\sigma_{xy}. Among the four 𝒯\mathcal{T}-broken descendants of Z3000 classified in Ref. [73] this signature selects Z300011 uniquely, and the representative mean-field spectrum of that descendant is fully gapped. Z300000 (Dirac) and Z300001,10 carry different signatures and are unrelated to the flux instability. The two runaway sectors thus admit explicit descendants of the same parent. The empty-plaquette VBS route leads to P5A, the plaquette descendant of Z3000 identified in Appendix G of Ref. [73], and the chirality route leads to Z300011.

Adding m​𝒫χm\mathcal{P}_{\chi} to the full Z3000(sH)(s_{H})+DM Bloch Hamiltonian opens a full gap close to 4​|m|4|m|, for example 0.390.39–0.400.40 at |m|=0.1|m|=0.1. The BdG Chern number of the occupied Majorana bands, evaluated over the full zone with the lattice formula of Ref. [29] with determinant link variables [its Eq. (16)], is

CBdG=−4​sgn​(m)(sH=0​–​0.2,d=0​ and ​0.6).C_{\rm BdG}=-4\,\mathrm{sgn}(m)\qquad(s_{H}=0\text{--}0.2,\ d=0\text{ and }0.6). (19)

On a cylinder the gap hosts four chiral Majorana branches per edge with opposite chirality on the two edges (±4\pm 4 signed zero-energy crossings). For sH>0s_{H}>0 the Higgs condensate leaves a gapped ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} gauge field, and the chiral central charge of the state is c=CBdG/2=∓2c=C_{\rm BdG}/2=\mp 2 [61, 93], two valleys times two spins of the same chirality. At sH=0s_{H}=0 the same bands carry the SU(2) invariant gauge group, and projection then gives an SU(2)1 chiral spin liquid with |c|=1|c|=1 instead. The quantized value below therefore requires the Higgsed phase, and temperatures below both the Chern gap and the ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} flux gap, which is small near the critical point. Then

κx​yT=c​π2​kB23​h=∓2​π2​kB23​h\frac{\kappa_{xy}}{T}=c\,\frac{\pi^{2}k_{B}^{2}}{3h}=\mp 2\,\frac{\pi^{2}k_{B}^{2}}{3h} (20)

is the T→0T\to 0 thermal Hall coefficient of the minority phase, ∓1.9×10−12\mp 1.9\times 10^{-12} W K-2 per layer. Finite-TT bulk corrections are exponentially small in the gap. The quantized value requires the ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} gauge field to be deconfined and gapped. The sign of κx​y\kappa_{xy} follows that of the scalar chirality and of the accompanying zz magnetization; at mean field Mz​κx​y>0M_{z}\kappa_{xy}>0 (Appendix J). The PSG class does not fix the Chern number. The Z300011 family of the locked PSG is 42-dimensional and contains other topological sectors separated by gap closings. Along 32 random 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd rays the minimal state m​𝒫χm\mathcal{P}_{\chi} keeps CBdG=−4​sgn​(m)C_{\rm BdG}=-4\,\mathrm{sgn}(m) at half its amplitude on all rays and at equal amplitude on 31, and on every ray whose phase boundary is determined its gapped component extends to 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd admixtures comparable to or larger than the flux mass (Appendix J). The weak uniform zz moment is DM-specific: it follows from the projected identity P⁡(J0​σz)=−P⁡(flux)P(J^{0}\sigma^{z})=-P({\rm flux}) of the spin–orbit-locked QBT (Sec. IX.2), vanishes in the spin-rotation-invariant limit, and is not a property of the Z300011 PSG class as such.

The spin-singlet Z3000 and Z300011 ansätze are seeds of the mean-field theory of the spin–orbit-locked problem and do not exhaust it. Besides the seven singlet amplitudes, the locked Z3000 PSG admits fourteen spin-triplet amplitudes in the buckled structure (two with D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} alone), and the Wick-induced DM operators lie inside this space and are purely triplet. Restricted self-consistency on a fixed Z3000 background changes the in-plane DM operator by 0.06%0.06\% in norm and leaves the nodes gapless (Appendix J).

X.3 Which VBS: plaquette selection

The VBSx/VBSy degeneracy has two layers. In the quadratic sector it is exact. The valley charge Q=∫Tr⁡[𝒳¯​γ0​μy​𝒳]Q=\int\mathrm{Tr}[\bar{\mathcal{X}}\gamma^{0}\mu^{y}\mathcal{X}] generates a U​(1)valleyU(1)_{\rm valley} under which (Vx,Vy)(V_{x},V_{y}) rotates with charge 2 while the flux mass, 𝒪DM\mathcal{O}_{\rm DM} and the kinetic term are singlets, as follows from exponentiating the bilinears of Sec. IV. No zeroth-gradient bilinear, and no mean-field effect of the linearized continuum theory, can therefore split the doublet. The splitting enters through the irrelevant gradient terms of the lattice theory, the O⁡(k2)O(k^{2}) band curvature and the O⁡(k)O(k) form factors of the DM and VBS vertices, which break U​(1)valleyU(1)_{\rm valley} and are contained in the lattice determinant computed below. The quartic sector is not fully valley-symmetric, since 99 of the 1414 invariant couplings preserve U​(1)valleyU(1)_{\rm valley} and 55 break it (the charges appear as singular values 4,2,2,2,24,2,2,2,2 of the generator’s action), the Vx​VyV_{x}V_{y}-type quartic among them. A Vx​VyV_{x}V_{y} seed feeds the combinations Vx±VyV_{x}\pm V_{y} with opposite rates through the one-loop source mixing. On the majority ray the tie is restored dynamically, so the degeneracy along the flow from random seeds is an emergent property of that ray. Selection within the doublet therefore has two contributions: flow amplification of valley-breaking quartic seeds, which we estimate at tree level below, and the lattice determinant. We compute the determinant contribution and the bare valley-breaking couplings.

Which anisotropies are allowed is fixed by the locked group. On the (Vx,Vy)=|V|(cos⁡θ,sin⁡θ)(V_{x},V_{y})=|V|(\cos\theta,\sin\theta) circle the tables of Sec. IV give S^4:(Vx,Vy)→(Vy,Vx)\hat{S}_{4}:(V_{x},V_{y})\to(V_{y},V_{x}), a swap, i.e. a mirror along the (1,1)(1,1) diagonal, σ^x​y,σ^x​y¯:(Vx,Vy)→(−Vy,−Vx)\hat{\sigma}_{xy},\hat{\sigma}_{x\bar{y}}:(V_{x},V_{y})\to(-V_{y},-V_{x}), and G^x:(Vx,Vy)→−(Vx,Vy)\hat{G}_{x}:(V_{x},V_{y})\to-(V_{x},V_{y}). The first three are mirrors along the diagonals, and G^x\hat{G}_{x} is the rotation by π\pi that they generate. Hence

F⁡(θ)=F0+b2​sin⁡2​θ+a4​cos⁡4​θ+⋯,F(\theta)=F_{0}+b_{2}\sin 2\theta+a_{4}\cos 4\theta+\cdots, (21)

with cos⁡2​θ\cos 2\theta and sin⁡4​θ\sin 4\theta forbidden. Higher allowed harmonics such as sin⁡6​θ\sin 6\theta appear at higher order in mm and are negligible at the parameters below. The four high-symmetry directions are lattice states, identified by projecting explicit bond patterns onto the continuum masses. The axes are the two columnar dimerizations, (−1)ix(-1)^{i_{x}} on xx bonds giving −Vx-V_{x} and (−1)iy(-1)^{i_{y}} on yy bonds giving +Vy+V_{y}. The diagonal θ=π/4\theta=\pi/4 is the empty-plaquette pattern PeP_{\rm e}, a bond strengthening alternating between the two sublattices of void squares (the singlet-plaquette state on empty squares), which as a lattice operator equals the columnar combination −colx+coly-{\rm col}_{x}+{\rm col}_{y}. The diagonal θ=3​π/4\theta=3\pi/4 is the full-plaquette pattern PfP_{\rm f}, the alternation of the two dimer-carrying crossed-square sublattices, equal to +colx+coly+{\rm col}_{x}+{\rm col}_{y}, and θ=−π/4\theta=-\pi/4 is its partner −Pf-P_{\rm f}. Thus, b2b_{2} splits empty from full plaquette, which on the Shastry–Sutherland lattice are inequivalent phases, while a4a_{4} controls diagonals versus axes. With both harmonics present the extrema of Eq. (21) satisfy cos⁡2​θ​(b2−4​a4​sin⁡2​θ)=0\cos 2\theta\,(b_{2}-4a_{4}\sin 2\theta)=0. The diagonals are always stationary, while the columnar axes are stationary only at b2=0b_{2}=0. For a4<0a_{4}<0 and |b2|<4​|a4||b_{2}|<4|a_{4}| the minima lie off the diagonals at sin⁡2​θ=b2/(4​a4)\sin 2\theta=b_{2}/(4a_{4}), and they approach the columnar axes as |b2|/|a4|→0|b_{2}|/|a_{4}|\to 0.

Both signs follow from the lattice determinant (Fig. 4) of the Bloch-reduced π\pi-flux ansatz plus the Wick-induced DM operator at lattice amplitude dd, perturbed by m⁡[cos⁡θ⁡(−colx)+sin⁡θ​coly]m[\cos\theta\,(-{\rm col}_{x})+\sin\theta\,{\rm col}_{y}], with F⁡(θ)F(\theta) evaluated on momentum grids up to 2002200^{2}. The results are identical for both in-plane DM textures and even under d→−dd\to-d. We find

a4>0(∝m4),b2<0(∝d4),a_{4}>0\ (\propto m^{4}),\qquad b_{2}<0\ (\propto d^{4}), (22)

for m≳3×10−3m\gtrsim 3\times 10^{-3} (smaller mm is treated below), so a4>0a_{4}>0 puts minima on the diagonals, and b2<0b_{2}<0 selects sin⁡2​θ=+1\sin 2\theta=+1, the empty-square plaquette direction, which is the plaquette channel of the pure Shastry–Sutherland model [17]. A=4​λπ2​(1+ϵ)​E​(κ)−K⁡(κ)(1+ϵ)2=2​λ3π​t2​[1−154​λ2t2+O⁡(λ4t4)],A=\frac{4\lambda}{\pi^{2}}\,\frac{(1+\epsilon)E(\kappa)-K(\kappa)}{(1+\epsilon)^{2}}=\frac{2\lambda^{3}}{\pi t^{2}}\Bigl[1-\frac{15}{4}\frac{\lambda^{2}}{t^{2}}+O\Bigl(\frac{\lambda^{4}}{t^{4}}\Bigr)\Bigr], (25)

The lattice b2b_{2} approaches Eq. (23) to 10−410^{-4} for m≤1.6×10−3m\leq 1.6\times 10^{-3}. For m≪λm\ll\lambda both harmonics have a controlled form. The touching also generates an infrared cos⁡4​θ\cos 4\theta term, fourth order in the dx​yd_{xy} form factor, so that a4=−(3​λ5/16​π​t4)​m2+a4(4)​m4a_{4}=-(3\lambda^{5}/16\pi t^{4})\,m^{2}+a_{4}^{(4)}m^{4} to leading order in λ/t\lambda/t, with a4(4)=0.039​ta_{4}^{(4)}=0.039\,t at d=0.6d=0.6, and a4a_{4} changes sign near m≃7×10−4m\simeq 7\times 10^{-4}; a4∝m4a_{4}\propto m^{4} holds for m≳3×10−3m\gtrsim 3\times 10^{-3}. It therefore grows without bound as m→0m\to 0, logarithmically, provided the Higgs splitting δ′\delta^{\prime} and the temperature lie below the gap 2​m​t2mt. Within the determinant contribution the minima at T∗⁣∗T^{**} are therefore the empty-plaquette pair θ=π/4, 5​π/4\theta=\pi/4,\,5\pi/4 (the two void sublattices), a two-state Ising order parameter. The total selection also receives the flow-amplified valley-breaking quartic seeds. Their tree-level estimate, given below, is larger than the determinant contribution, but after the running to λ\lambda it need not be. If the thermal transition is continuous, 2D Ising universality is expected, but the transition temperature and its order are not computed here. Since the Wick-induced DM operator is held fixed while the singlet links are modulated, the result is a determinant contribution, and the self-consistent total energy is not computed.

In the full Z3000(sH)(s_{H})+DM Bloch background, with the Higgs-deviation scale sHs_{H} of Eq. (18), the global minimum is located directly, because the sign of b2b_{2} alone is not a phase criterion once a4<0a_{4}<0. The forbidden harmonics again vanish, b2b_{2} stays between −1.88-1.88 and −2.05×10−7t-2.05\times 10^{-7}\,t for sH≤0.1s_{H}\leq 0.1, and the two empty-plaquette states remain the global minima for sH≤0.055s_{H}\leq 0.055 (at m=0.05m=0.05, d=0.6d=0.6). This range covers most of the open-QBT window at d=0.6d=0.6, which extends to sH≃0.03s_{H}\simeq 0.03–0.080.08 for the gauge-driven flow (ℓ∗≃0.6\ell^{*}\simeq 0.6–1.61.6, depending on the screening and on the upper energy of the quadratic regime), and to smaller sHs_{H} at the material λ\lambda. At larger sHs_{H}, a4a_{4} changes sign near sH≃0.055s_{H}\simeq 0.055, and once 4​|a4|4|a_{4}| exceeds |b2||b_{2}|, near sH≃0.057s_{H}\simeq 0.057, the minima leave the diagonal. They lie 12∘12^{\circ} from the nearest columnar axis at sH=0.06s_{H}=0.06, within 3∘3^{\circ} of it at sH=0.07s_{H}=0.07, and within 0.5∘0.5^{\circ} for sH≥0.1s_{H}\geq 0.1. Within the determinant, the empty-plaquette selection is therefore a near-critical statement, and the near-critical regime is where the phase diagram proposed in Ref. [19] places the empty-plaquette phase, next to the antiferromagnet (see below). Deeper in the Higgsed phase, where no weak-coupling instability exists, the same determinant favors columnar-like directions.

The determinant result is compared here with the selection already present in the Heisenberg problem. Reference [68] describes the Néel–VBS transition on this lattice in monopole language, with the VBS doublet (vx,vy)(v_{x},v_{y}) combined into a complex monopole field MM. There the double-monopole term λ2​Re​M2\lambda_{2}\,{\rm Re}\,M^{2}, the most relevant monopole perturbation allowed on this lattice, breaks the U(1) phase rotation of MM down to ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2}. For λ2>0\lambda_{2}>0 it selects the square (empty) plaquette state, with the twofold-degenerate order parameter Im​M{\rm Im}\,M. At the transition Im​M{\rm Im}\,M is argued to combine with the Néel vector into an O(4) vector, with an emergent O(4) symmetry in place of the SO(5) of the theory without that term. Tensor-network calculations for the pure Shastry–Sutherland model find the same empty-plaquette phase [17]. The harmonic b2​sin⁡2​θb_{2}\sin 2\theta of Eq. (21) plays the role of that selector in the fermionic language, reducing the (Vx,Vy)(V_{x},V_{y}) circle to one diagonal pair, ±Pe\pm P_{\rm e} or ±Pf\pm P_{\rm f}. The (Vx,Vy)(V_{x},V_{y}) doublet is the counterpart of (vx,vy)(v_{x},v_{y}), and hence of MM, in Ref. [68]. The empty plaquette lies at θ=π/4\theta=\pi/4 here and at vx=−vyv_{x}=-v_{y} there, where Re​M2=2​vx​vy<0{\rm Re}\,M^{2}=2v_{x}v_{y}<0, so b2<0b_{2}<0 corresponds to λ2>0\lambda_{2}>0. In the material the Heisenberg couplings, with J′/J≃0.6J^{\prime}/J\simeq 0.6, are the dominant selector, whereas the DM couplings enter the determinant only through dd, with |DΣ′|∼2×10−3​J|D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}|\sim 2\times 10^{-3}J. The empty-plaquette selection therefore comes from the Heisenberg couplings, and the determinant adds only a small correction of the same sign. Its own correction has the sign of the Heisenberg selection. Because b2b_{2} is even in dd, this correction is the same in the two inversion twins of the crystal [112], which reverse the sign of all in-plane DM components. The absence of a d2d^{2} term in b2b_{2}, which scales as d4d^{4} down to d=0.01d=0.01 for m≫λm\gg\lambda and as |d|3|d|^{3} in the logarithmic regime (Appendix F), together with the vanishing of the dimer-bond amplitude ⟨fi†​fj⟩dimer=0\langle f^{\dagger}_{i}f^{\vphantom{\dagger}}_{j}\rangle_{\rm dimer}=0 on the π\pi-flux state (the bipartite chiral selection rule of Sec. V.3), makes the DM channel the only Shastry–Sutherland-aware term in the π\pi-flux determinant at this level. In the Z3000(sH)(s_{H}) background the dimer and orthogonal-dimer amplitudes add a DM-independent contribution, b2≃−1.0×10−4sH4tb_{2}\simeq-1.0\times 10^{-4}s_{H}^{4}\,t at m=0.05m=0.05 and small sHs_{H}. It has the same sign and dominates the DM channel for sH≳0.4​ds_{H}\gtrsim 0.4\,d. Exchange fluctuations beyond the determinant renormalize b2b_{2}, and a sign change would require them to overcome the computed channel.

Tree-level quartic seeds. The bare quartic couplings follow at tree level from projecting the exchange Hamiltonian of Eq. (1), written in terms of the partons, onto the eight QBT modes at zeroth order in gradients (Appendix K). We denote by g⁡(θ)g(\theta) the resulting coupling in the VBS channel along θ\theta, with g>0g>0 attractive. The JJ–J′J^{\prime} exchange gives a valley-symmetric seed for every J′/JJ^{\prime}/J. Each nearest-neighbor bond alone breaks U​(1)valleyU(1)_{\rm valley}, but the four nearest-neighbor bond classes cancel in the symmetric sum. The dimer bonds preserve it, and so do diagonal couplings of any range, which at Γ\Gamma connect the same sublattice pairs. The exchange gives g=J′g=J^{\prime} at every θ\theta, an attractive Néelz channel (+1.51​J+1.51J at J′/J=0.63J^{\prime}/J=0.63) and a repulsive flux channel (−1.01​J-1.01J). The valley-breaking seed comes from the DM exchange. The in-plane inter-dimer components D′∥,sD^{\prime}_{\parallel,s} and D′∥,nsD^{\prime}_{\parallel,ns} break U​(1)valleyU(1)_{\rm valley} but contribute nothing on the VBS circle. This is required by the inversion twins, which reverse these components and map each plaquette pattern to itself. The intra-dimer DD drops out of the QBT. The out-of-plane component gives

g⁡(θ)=J′+2​D⟂′​sin⁡2​θ,g(\theta)=J^{\prime}+2D^{\prime}_{\perp}\sin 2\theta, (26)

so that g⁡(Pe)−g⁡(Pf)=4​D⟂′g(P_{\rm e})-g(P_{\rm f})=4D^{\prime}_{\perp}, with D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} normalized as in Table 1. The term exists only on the spin–orbit-locked QBT modes. On the sixteen Dirac modes the same operator has no component on the VBS circle, in line with the inertness of D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} above T∗T^{*} (Sec. VII).

The fractional anisotropy of Eq. (26) is 2​|D⟂′|/J′≃0.042|D^{\prime}_{\perp}|/J^{\prime}\simeq 0.04–0.080.08 for |D⟂′|=0.10|D^{\prime}_{\perp}|=0.10–0.180.18 meV. The corresponding ratio for the determinant in the band-touching channel is A/Ciso=(λ2/2​t2)​[1+O⁡(λ2/t2)]=1.29×10−3A/C_{\rm iso}=(\lambda^{2}/2t^{2})[1+O(\lambda^{2}/t^{2})]=1.29\times 10^{-3} at d=0.6d=0.6, where Ciso≃4​λ/πC_{\rm iso}\simeq 4\lambda/\pi is the coefficient of the isotropic m2​ln⁡(1/m)m^{2}\ln(1/m) term, and it falls as d2d^{2} toward the material value. It is a ratio of the singular parts; the full ratio b2/Δ​Fisob_{2}/\Delta F_{\rm iso}, which includes the regular parts, is (1CLOSE(1–OPEN2)×10−42)\times 10^{-4} at d=0.6d=0.6. In the one-loop flow the tree-level seed lies in the VBS basin (Sec. X.1). Without the running described below, the vertex of the plaquette pattern favored by D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} outgrows the other by Δ​ln⁡Γ≃2.0\Delta\ln\Gamma\simeq 2.0 for |D⟂′|=0.10|D^{\prime}_{\perp}|=0.10 meV and ≃3.3\simeq 3.3 for 0.180.18 meV, independently of the seed scale (a directional measure, since the tree seeds themselves diverge only after ℓ∗≃40\ell^{*}\simeq 40–160160). At tree level the DM-induced selection within the doublet is therefore set by the sign of D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}, with the determinant a subleading correction; the running described below can reverse this ordering. That sign is D⟂′<0D^{\prime}_{\perp}<0 by the NMR determination of Ref. [63] and by Table II of Ref. [77] (Sec. II); this sign favors the full-plaquette pair ±Pf\pm P_{\rm f}. Reference [14] read the opposite sign, which would favor ±Pe\pm P_{\rm e}, from the far-infrared analysis of Ref. [11], a discrepancy that Ref. [77] attributes to conventions. The seed exists only on the band-touching modes, i.e. for DΣ′≠0D^{\prime}_{\Sigma}\neq 0 and below T∗T^{*}. Perturbatively, in the gapped plaquette phases, a global π\pi spin rotation about an in-plane axis reverses D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} and leaves the exchange invariant, so an energy difference odd in D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} is at least of order D⟂′​D∥2D^{\prime}_{\perp}D_{\parallel}^{2} there. The selection that the pure Shastry–Sutherland model makes beyond tree level is not computed.

Running to the band-touching scale. The seeds are defined at the lattice scale Λ∼J′\Lambda\sim J^{\prime}–JJ. Between Λ\Lambda and λ\lambda, over L=ln⁡(Λ/λ)≃7L=\ln(\Lambda/\lambda)\simeq 7–99, they run in the Dirac regime with the scaling dimensions of four-fermion operators at the SO(5) fixed point. These dimensions are obtained at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) for all 336 gauge-invariant local four-fermion operators, from the fermion self-energy, one-gauge-line exchange between every pair of legs, and the two-gauge-line annihilation of flux-singlet pairs and, through the induced three-gauge vertex, of gauge-current pairs (Appendix K). The same rules give the bilinear dimensions of Appendix O and, in their abelian form, agree with the large-NN QED3 four-fermion dimensions of Ref. [15], including the flavor-singlet pair whose mixing with F2F^{2}, the square of the gauge field strength, enters through the current square.
