    The U800 monopole classification (Appendix N) is kinematic. The scaling dimension of the allowed SO(5)-singlet monopole in the present theory is not computed; the QED3 value with four two-component flavors is about 11 [6, 91], and the monopole’s topological phases are taken from the mean-field spinon state.

  • •

    The disorder flows are evaluated at O⁡(Δ2,Δ/N)O(\Delta^{2},\Delta/N), with Δ\Delta the disorder strength. The dimensions of the 𝒯\mathcal{T}-even Higgs bilinears and of the constraint field, which carry random fields and random TcT_{c} at the multicritical point, receive corrections of order one at N=12N=12 and are not controlled; the vacancy results are mean field. The strengths of the material’s disorder are estimates from Curie tails, pressure inhomogeneity and strain, the stability of a diffusive spinon regime is not settled, and the domain-glass conclusion holds for strictly two-dimensional random fields or for substituted crystals.

  • •

    If the plaquette phase lowers the tetragonal symmetry, additional DM components become symmetry-allowed and are not classified here; the symmetry of that phase is not settled (Sec. II). The same holds above the monoclinic onset at 4.04.0–5.05.0 GPa [71, 134].

XV Conclusions

We obtain the following results for the Shastry–Sutherland Dirac spin liquids with the DM couplings of SrCu2(BO3)2.

  1. 1.

    DM interactions cannot gap the spinons or destabilize the SO(5) point above T∗T^{*} at linear order. No symmetry-allowed local gauge-singlet fermion mass is generated at any order. The largest inter-dimer coupling, D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}, induces at linear order only a flavored spin-2 current, irrelevant at any unitary critical point, with ΔOB=3.32\Delta_{O_{B}}=3.32 at leading order. At second order the DM couplings seed the rank-2 SO(5) tensor, easy-axis from D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} and easy-plane from λ\lambda at mean field; the tensor is irrelevant at leading order in 1/N1/N and, if the fuzzy-sphere dimension applies, acts at a scale of order T∗T^{*} or above, up to about 11 K. The in-plane couplings generate one conserved-current operator of dimension exactly 2, with RG eigenvalue 1 and scale T∗≃0.03T^{*}\simeq 0.03–0.170.17 K for the DFT couplings. The intra-dimer DD also induces Yukawa couplings to the critical Higgs fields, which start at 6×10−46\times 10^{-4}–2×10−22\times 10^{-2} of the Yukawa coupling that bounds the pseudocritical window and, barring a cancellation among the Z3000 amplitudes, remain subleading within it.

  2. 2.

    Below T∗T^{*} the spinons form a quadratic band touching with two weak-coupling instability sectors at one loop. Near the critical pressure the Dirac cones reconstruct into a chirally protected dd-wave band touching whose only gauge-singlet gap channels are the valence-bond doublet and the scalar chirality, with Néel gapping excluded kinematically. The one-loop flow makes a fivefold sector containing valence-bond order the majority outcome, also for seeds restricted to the gauge-singlet couplings, and the seed of the material exchange lies in that basin, also after the O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) running. The gauge interaction, including its dynamical screening by the band touching, the transverse field and the Higgs polarization, lies in the same one-loop basin, but only 22–4%4\% of its norm from its boundary, so gauge exchange alone does not decide the outcome; it sets the order-of-magnitude one-loop estimate T∗⁣∗≃(0.03CLOSET^{**}\simeq(0.03–OPEN0.1)​λ0.1)\lambda. A gapped chiral ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2} liquid with CBdG=∓4C_{\rm BdG}=\mp 4 and quantized thermal Hall conductance is the minority outcome.

  3. 3.

    The DM correction to the plaquette pattern is a small bias whose direction is not fixed. A seed linear in D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}, g⁡(Pe)−g⁡(Pf)=4​D⟂′g(P_{\rm e})-g(P_{\rm f})=4D^{\prime}_{\perp} at tree level, and the lattice determinant, of opposite preference, compete within the Ising plaquette pair. The seed’s selector does not run at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N), while the isotropic valence-bond attraction grows through its SO(5)-singlet part, whose running at the O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) value of Δσ\Delta_{\sigma} is dominated by the constraint-field mode, so at the band-touching scale the DM correction is a bias of at most of order 10−410^{-4} and the flow ends on the VBS ray. Which of the two leads depends on the Higgs sector of the singlet channel, which is not controlled at N=12N=12, so the direction is not determined at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N). For D⟂′<0D^{\prime}_{\perp}<0, the sign found by NMR, the seed favors the full plaquette.

  4. 4.

    Magnetic fields and disorder act selectively. A field along [100][100] activates a Néel mass at linear order and a field along [001][001] does not, a selection rule of the lattice symmetry that holds in the dimer phase as well. Non-magnetic, time-reversal-invariant quenched disorder in zero field couples a relevant random field to the plaquette doublet and, to all orders in the disorder and in 1/N1/N, none to the chirality; at the multicritical point random TcT_{c} is relevant at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) and the 𝒯\mathcal{T}-even Higgs bilinears also receive random fields, but the dimensions behind both statements are not controlled at N=12N=12.

The limitations are those listed in Sec. XIV. The large-NN numbers are qualitative at N=12N=12, and the crossover prefactor and the field-induced coefficients are mean field. The QBT window is conditional on proximity to the critical pressure and on a strictly two-dimensional sample, whereas the interlayer coupling of the material exceeds T∗T^{*} and the samples measured so far order above 11 K. The running of the plaquette correction is O⁡(1/N)O(1/N), with an uncontrolled Higgs sector in the SO(5)-singlet channel, and the sign of D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} rests on one NMR determination, with an apparent far-infrared discrepancy that has been attributed to conventions. The disorder verdict depends on the correlation structure and the magnetic character of the material’s randomness.

Four measurements bear on the scenario. A 11B NMR comparison of 𝑩|[100]\bm{B}\parallel[100] and 𝑩|[001]\bm{B}\parallel[001] at matched g​μB​Bg\mu_{B}B between 2.42.4 and 2.82.8 GPa, below the field-induced transition, tests the orientation-selective Néel response. Zero-field calorimetry near the critical pressure would test the finite spinon density of states in samples in which the pseudocritical regime survives down to T∗T^{*}. It requires temperatures below about 0.030.03–0.170.17 K. The linear term is approached only near 0.02​T∗0.02\,T^{*}, comparable to T∗⁣∗≃(0.008CLOSET^{**}\simeq(0.008–OPEN0.025)​T∗0.025)\,T^{*}, so the instability may preempt it. In the existing samples, order sets in above 11 K (Sec. XIII.2). A zero-field thermal Hall measurement under pressure below T∗⁣∗T^{**}, after cooling in a weak cc-axis field of either sign, would detect the chiral minority phase if it forms. A null result is the outcome expected for the majority basin. An independent determination of the sign of D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} fixes the direction of the DM correction to the plaquette pattern only once the constraint-field dimension Δσ\Delta_{\sigma} and the determinant ratio are known, since they decide whether the seed or the determinant leads. The absence of gauge-singlet masses requires only the time-reversal oddness of the Néel and chirality masses, the lattice parities of the spin-singlet VBS masses, which locking cannot change, and the absence of quantum-spin-Hall masses in the SU(2) theory. It therefore carries over to any lattice realization of this gauge theory whose SO(5) vector consists of Néel and VBS order parameters. The locked-symmetry classification applies to other Dirac-spin-liquid candidates with spin–orbit coupling, and on the Shastry–Sutherland lattice it also delivers the complete gauge-singlet bilinear tables without derivatives (Tables 2 and 3). These complement the published gauge-adjoint classifications of Refs. [118, 27].

Appendix A Conventions

This appendix collects the conventions used in the analytic and numerical calculations.

Spin axes. A uniform lattice Zeeman field along a physical axis projects onto the single bilinear γ0​σa\gamma^{0}\sigma^{a}, and a staggered one with the Néel pattern onto the single bilinear μy​σa\mu^{y}\sigma^{a}. The component along xx enters with the sign opposite to those along yy and zz, so the spin label of the bilinears in Tables 2–4 and in Eq. (7) is related to the physical axes by x→−xx\to-x. The field and moment directions of Sec. XI and Table 7 are physical and include this sign.

Energies. The lattice Majorana Bloch kernels are built by applying a local antisymmetric-bilinear map to the kinetic terms of each ansatz. They are used for number-conserving quantities only, namely spectra, susceptibilities, and band-touching matrices, for which they agree with the complex-fermion construction of the same states. The Majorana kernel H=i​∑K​LAK​L​MK​MLH=\mathrm{i}\sum_{KL}A_{KL}M_{K}M_{L} with {MK,ML}=δK​L\{M_{K},M_{L}\}=\delta_{KL} has excitation energies 2​eig​(i​A)2\,{\rm eig}(\mathrm{i}A). All lattice energies quoted in this paper, in units of tt or in kelvin, are physical. Kelvin values carry the mean-field prefactor uncertainty stated in Sec. IX.1.

Published tables. Figure 4 of Ref. [118] contains three rows μy​σb​γμ\mu^{y}\sigma^{b}\gamma^{\mu} with μ=0,x,y\mu=0,x,y (printed there as μy​σa​γμ\mu^{y}\sigma^{a}\gamma^{\mu}), where bb is the spin index. The caption states that the entries give the transformation of the trace Tr⁡[σa​𝒳¯​Γj​γμ​𝒳]\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\,\Gamma^{j}\gamma^{\mu}\mathcal{X}]. The printed 𝒯\mathcal{T} signs of these rows are (+,−,−)(+,-,-). The corresponding Hermitian operators transform under 𝒯\mathcal{T} with the opposite signs (−,+,+)(-,+,+), for all nine combinations of the gauge index aa and the spin index bb, in agreement with Table 3 of Ref. [27], whose GxG_{x} signs (+,+,−)(+,+,-) also agree with ours. A phase convention for 𝒯\mathcal{T} cannot produce this flip, because it is a relative sign within one gauge-adjoint SO(5) multiplet. The conserved charge of the generator μz​σb\mu^{z}\sigma^{b} is 𝒯\mathcal{T}-even, and it rotates μx​γμ\mu^{x}\gamma^{\mu} into μy​σb​γμ\mu^{y}\sigma^{b}\gamma^{\mu} through [μz​σb,μx]=2​i​μy​σb[\mu^{z}\sigma^{b},\mu^{x}]=2\mathrm{i}\mu^{y}\sigma^{b}. Because 𝒯\mathcal{T} is antiunitary, the factor i\mathrm{i} requires the two rows to carry opposite 𝒯\mathcal{T} signs, whereas Fig. 4 of Ref. [118] prints equal signs. We therefore regard the printed signs of these three rows there as misprints. All Lagrangian-relevant rows and all gauge-singlet statements are unaffected.

Appendix B Vanishing of the SO(5)-adjoint scalars

Write the sixteen Majorana fields as ηK\eta_{K} and any bilinear as 𝒪=i​ηT​A​η\mathcal{O}=\mathrm{i}\,\eta^{T}A\,\eta with AA real antisymmetric. In the Majorana basis the matrices representing γ0​M\gamma^{0}M for M∈{Tj}M\in\{T^{j}\}, the would-be adjoint scalars, are symmetric. Their antisymmetric part, the only part that survives between Grassmann fields, therefore vanishes identically. For M∈{Γj,𝟙}M\in\{\Gamma^{j},\mathds{1}\} the matrices are antisymmetric and survive. The counting 6+30=366+30=36 then follows from dim[antisym⁡(16)]=120\dim[\mathrm{antisym}(16)]=120 reduced by gauge invariance. Physically, for Nf=2N_{f}=2 valleys with an SU(2) gauge redundancy, the SO(5)-adjoint (quantum-spin-Hall-type) masses exist only as gauge adjoints, and the reality structure removes their gauge-singlet projections. The spin-carrying Néel masses belong to the SO(5) vector and survive.

Appendix C DM textures

The allowed DM components are the null space of the invariance condition 𝑫O⁡(i)​O​(j)=det(O)​O​𝑫i​j\bm{D}_{O(i)O(j)}=\det(O)\,O\,\bm{D}_{ij} over one magnetic cell, for each bond class. In the high-temperature structure the intra-dimer bonds carry 0 components, the inter-dimer bonds carry 1 (D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}, alternating as in Table 1), and both the orthogonal diagonals of the crossed squares and the diagonals of the empty squares carry 0. In the buckled structure the intra-dimer bonds carry 1 component, in-plane, perpendicular to the dimer, and staggered between orientations. This pattern matches Supplementary Eq. (4) of Ref. [94] in the relative sign of the two dimer orientations. The inter-dimer bonds carry 3 components. The orthogonal diagonals of the crossed squares carry 1, in-plane and perpendicular to the bond, and the diagonals of the empty squares carry 2, both in-plane. These next-nearest-neighbor couplings are of negligible range and are not considered further. The Romhányi frame maps to ours by x^R=(x^+y^)/2\hat{x}_{R}=(\hat{x}{+}\hat{y})/\sqrt{2}, y^R=(−x^+y^)/2\hat{y}_{R}=(-\hat{x}{+}\hat{y})/\sqrt{2}, with the sublattice dictionary A1=(A,A)A_{1}{=}(A,A), A2=(B,B)A_{2}{=}(B,B), B1=(B,A)B_{1}{=}(B,A), B2=(A,B)B_{2}{=}(A,B). With this mapping our reference vector 𝑫′\bm{D}^{\prime} on A1→B1A_{1}\to B_{1} (Table 1) coincides with that of Ref. [94], while our DD equals −D-D of Ref. [94]. The intra-dimer vectors of Fig. 1(a) therefore agree with Supplementary Fig. 2 of Ref. [94] only up to this overall sign. The combination D~∥=D∥,s′−(J′/2J)D\tilde{D}_{\parallel}=D^{\prime}_{\parallel,s}-(J^{\prime}/2J)D of Ref. [94] [Supplementary Eq. (12)] reads D~∥=D∥,s′+(J′/2J)D\tilde{D}_{\parallel}=D^{\prime}_{\parallel,s}+(J^{\prime}/2J)D in our convention.

Appendix D Mean-field decoupling of the DM interaction

For a bond ⟨i​j⟩\langle ij\rangle with DM vector 𝑫\bm{D}, using ∑a​bεc​a​b​σa⊗σb\sum_{ab}\varepsilon^{cab}\sigma^{a}\otimes\sigma^{b} Fierz identities and the singlet contractions ⟨fi​α†​fj​β⟩=χi​j​δα​β\langle f^{\dagger}_{i\alpha}f_{j\beta}\rangle=\chi_{ij}\delta_{\alpha\beta}, ⟨fi​α​fj​β⟩=Δi​j​εα​β\langle f_{i\alpha}f_{j\beta}\rangle=\Delta_{ij}\varepsilon_{\alpha\beta}, the Wick reduction of 𝑫⋅(𝑺i×𝑺j)\bm{D}\cdot(\bm{S}_{i}\times\bm{S}_{j}) gives the triplet hopping

with χi​j≡⟨fi​σ†​fj​σ⟩\chi_{ij}\equiv\langle f^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}f_{j\sigma}\rangle (no sum over σ\sigma), plus terms proportional to ⟨𝑺⟩=0\langle\bm{S}\rangle=0. The zero-mode matrix WW used throughout the appendices collects the zero-energy eigenvectors of the π\pi-flux Bloch kernel at the Dirac point. Summing the bond-resolved patterns of Table 1 over one cell with the π\pi-flux amplitudes χi​j=±i​χ0\chi_{ij}=\pm\mathrm{i}\chi_{0} and projecting onto the Dirac subspace yields Eq. (9), and a numerical Wick decoupling on a bulk cell confirms this coefficient and the vanishing contributions. Basin statistics in Sec. X.1 use 600 random unit seeds of strength 0.50.5 in bubble-log units. Two seeds do not diverge up to ℓ=60\ell=60 and are counted in neither basin. The lattice QBT curvature is isotropic between the two dd-wave channels, with the computed ratio r2≡c2/c1=0.9994r_{2}\equiv c_{2}/c_{1}=0.9994, as the continuum derivation assumes. A hypothetical anisotropy r2r_{2} up to 33, implemented by replacing the bracket in Eq. (33) by 𝟙⊗𝟙+w1​𝒜^1⊗𝒜^1+w2​𝒜^2⊗𝒜^2\mathds{1}\otimes\mathds{1}+w_{1}\hat{\mathcal{A}}_{1}\otimes\hat{\mathcal{A}}_{1}+w_{2}\hat{\mathcal{A}}_{2}\otimes\hat{\mathcal{A}}_{2} with angular weights wiw_{i}, raises the VBS fraction for a sample of 300300 seeds from 84%84\% (isotropic) to 8787–88%88\%, and the Néelz rate remains zero.

Only 6 of the 14 invariant quartics are gauge singlets. The 14-coupling flow describes the Higgsed (Z3000) phase, where all 14 are legitimate short-range couplings. At the π\pi-flux critical point only the gauge-singlet subset survives, and the screened color interaction of Appendix L lies inside it. The flow preserves this subset to 10−1510^{-15}, and 600 seeds drawn inside it (same measure and criterion as above) end on valence-bond order for 435435 (73%±2%73\%\pm 2\%), on the flux mass for 149149, and do not diverge for 1616.

For the abelian pair, (d) and (e) cancel and (f) and (g) vanish. For the random-λ\lambda vertex every diagram (d)–(g) contains W0​αi​W0=0W_{0}\alpha_{i}W_{0}=0, and the flow comes from (b) alone. Every self-energy diagram begins and ends on W0=P−​W0​P−W_{0}=P_{-}W_{0}P_{-}, so Σ=P−​Σ​P−\Sigma=P_{-}\Sigma P_{-} to all orders, z+z_{+} and vv do not run, and g=Δ​z+/(v2​z−)g=\Delta z_{+}/(v^{2}z_{-}) is proportional to the Born scattering rate in units of the energy. Its decrease, Eq. (27), is therefore a decrease of the scattering rate, independent of the normalization convention.

The random-DM vertex is valley-blind, so the per-valley 4×44\times 4 space closes. Written without normalization, W0=ax​σx+ay​σyW_{0}=a_{x}\sigma^{x}+a_{y}\sigma^{y} has W02=2​(𝟙−β​σz)W_{0}^{2}=2(\mathds{1}-\beta\sigma^{z}) and W0​ai​W0=0W_{0}a_{i}W_{0}=0 identically, and it is the one case with non-scalar Z=𝟙+2​κ​(𝟙−β​σz)Z=\mathds{1}+2\kappa(\mathds{1}-\beta\sigma^{z}). With R=P++P−/1+4​κR=P_{+}+P_{-}/\sqrt{1+4\kappa} one finds R​ai​R=ai/1+4​κRa_{i}R=a_{i}/\sqrt{1+4\kappa} but R​W0​R=W0/(1+4​κ)RW_{0}R=W_{0}/(1+4\kappa), hence Δeff=Δ/(1+4​κ)\Delta_{\rm eff}=\Delta/(1+4\kappa) and dΔλ/dℓ=−4Δλ2/(2π)=−2Δλ2/πd\Delta_{\lambda}/d\ell=-4\Delta_{\lambda}^{2}/(2\pi)=-2\Delta_{\lambda}^{2}/\pi, which is Eq. (27) for the variance of the unnormalized vertex W0W_{0}. The two statements describe the same flow in the two normalizations, a marginal irrelevance without a fixed line. Retaining the generated β​σz\beta\sigma^{z} frequency tensor explicitly as a coupling closes the same flow: only z−z_{-} runs, z˙−=2​Δ​z+/(π​v2)\dot{z}_{-}=2\Delta z_{+}/(\pi v^{2}) from ∑iW0​αi​Z​αi​W0=8​z+​P−\sum_{i}W_{0}\alpha_{i}Z\alpha_{i}W_{0}=8z_{+}P_{-}, and g⁡(ℓ)=g0/(1+2​g0​ℓ/π)g(\ell)=g_{0}/(1+2g_{0}\ell/\pi). The full 16×1616\times 16 tensor projection of every one-loop topology vanishes because each factor contains W0​αi​W0=0W_{0}\alpha_{i}W_{0}=0.

Multi-vertex flow of the matched DM covariance. The 36 gauge singlets are represented as 8×88\times 8 Hermitian matrices in the (Dirac, valley, spin) basis, a complex structure in which all 36 are number-conserving, and completed to the 64-dimensional ρa​μb​σc\rho^{a}\mu^{b}\sigma^{c} basis of u⁡(8)u(8), on which the three topologies close. The 28 gauge-charged elements are carried along. In units of Δ2/(2​π)\Delta^{2}/(2\pi) for trace-normalized vertices the multi-vertex flow gives potential +2+2, mass −2-2, abelian gauge 00, and random-λ\lambda vertex tensors 00 with normalization −2-2, in agreement with the values above. Matching proceeds bond by bond. For each of the 8 NN and 2 dimer bonds of the reference cell and each δ​Dα\delta D_{\alpha}, the Wick-decoupled quadratic operator is projected with the zero-mode matrix WW on the 36 singlets. On the NN bonds the projection has the same norm, 2.65×10−32.65\times 10^{-3} per unit DD, for every bond and component, and the dimer-bond operators have no projection. The covariance Δ0=∑c​c𝖳\Delta_{0}=\sum c\,c^{\sf T} of the projected vectors cc has rank 12 with a twelvefold degenerate spectrum. Its class weights are 1/21/2 (Jx,y​σaJ^{x,y}\sigma^{a}), 1/21/2 (γ0​μx,z​σa\gamma^{0}\mu^{x,z}\sigma^{a}), and 00 (masses, magnetization, μy\mu^{y}). The largest eigendirections of Δ˙\dot{\Delta} are pure singlets, and the generated mass diagonal is μx:μz=1:1\mu^{x}{:}\,\mu^{z}=1{:}1 with all other masses 00. Integrating from 0.05​Δ00.05\,\Delta_{0} to ℓ=80\ell=80 gives tr⁡Δ=0.050→0.130\operatorname{tr}\Delta=0.050\to 0.130, with weights random-λ\lambda 0.50→0.510.50\to 0.51, staggered density 0.50→0.330.50\to 0.33, masses 0→0.130\to 0.13, the remaining 0.040.04 in other 𝒯\mathcal{T}-even singlets, and gauge-charged 00 throughout. The growth of the zero-coefficient ensembles comes entirely from the generated VBS-mass directions. The DM-generated covariance is thus marginally relevant at one loop for every bond-uncorrelated ensemble and marginally irrelevant for the smooth (cell-correlated) one, Eq. (28) being the isotropic bond-uncorrelated case.

Gauge fluctuations at O⁡(1/N)O(1/N). The replicated critical theory is Sn=∑aS∗​[𝒳a,Aa,Φa]−12​∑a​bΔi​j​∫d2​r​𝑑τ​d​τ′​Oi​(𝒓,τ)a​Oj​(𝒓,τ′)bS_{n}=\sum_{a}S_{*}[\mathcal{X}_{a},A_{a},\Phi_{a}]-\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{ab}\Delta_{ij}\int d^{2}r\,d\tau\,d\tau^{\prime}\,O_{i}(\bm{r},\tau)_{a}O_{j}(\bm{r},\tau^{\prime})_{b}, with one gauge field and one pair of Higgs triplets per replica and OiO_{i} running over the 16 𝒯\mathcal{T}-even gauge singlets: the two VBS masses, the six spin currents γx,y​σa\gamma^{x,y}\sigma^{a}, the six staggered densities γ0​μx,z​σa\gamma^{0}\mu^{x,z}\sigma^{a} and the two VBS-rotation currents γx,y​μy\gamma^{x,y}\mu^{y}. In the 8×88\times 8 basis time reversal is Θ=ρy​μy​σy\Theta=\rho^{y}\mu^{y}\sigma^{y} followed by complex conjugation, which reproduces the parities of Table 2 and H⁡(𝒌)→H⁡(−𝒌)H(\bm{k})\to H(-\bm{k}). For exchange disorder the covariance lives on the four spin singlets and has three invariants under the layer group, Δ+\Delta_{+}, Δ−\Delta_{-} and ΔJ\Delta_{J}, the plaquette components forming two one-dimensional representations; for DM disorder the locked group leaves 24 invariants on the 16 channels.

The gauge line is replica diagonal, so at O⁡(Δ/N)O(\Delta/N) it dresses one end of a disorder line at a time: vertex correction plus self-energy, which for a static insertion have the same logarithm as at zero momentum. With the rules of Appendix O a mass vertex has v=8​Cg​(3−ζ)/(π2​N)v=8C_{g}(3-\zeta)/(\pi^{2}N) and a density or spatial-current vertex v=8​Cg​(1−3​ζ)/(3​π2​N)=−sv=8C_{g}(1-3\zeta)/(3\pi^{2}N)=-s, so the dimensions entering Eq. (29) are 2−64​Cg/(3​π2​N)2-64C_{g}/(3\pi^{2}N) for the VBS and Néel masses and 22 for all 30 current components, independent of ζ\zeta. At O⁡(Δ2)O(\Delta^{2}) the only graphs beyond the free kernel are fermion loops tied to the external line by gauge propagators (Fig. 6(h),(i)), since loops tied by disorder lines alone carry a free replica sum. Charge conjugation removes the loops with vertex sets {m,m,A}\{m,m,A\}, {j,j,A}\{j,j,A\} and {j,A,A}\{j,A,A\}, and the zero-momentum current insertion on {j,m,A}\{j,m,A\} vanishes by the Ward identity. The remaining triangle, a zero-momentum mass with a random vector potential or potential and one gauge line, is parity odd and transverse, hence independent of the gauge parameter, and changes the mass vertex by κ​g​d​ℓ\kappa g\,d\ell per unit variance with κA=−8F/(2πN)\kappa_{A}=-8F/(2\pi N) and κV=+8F/(2πN)\kappa_{V}=+8F/(2\pi N), where FF is the flavor trace of the loop. In QED3, F=NF=N for TX=TY=σaT_{X}=T_{Y}=\sigma^{a}, so that the triangles add 8​gt​gA−8​gt​gv8g_{t}g_{A}-8g_{t}g_{v} to π​βt\pi\beta_{t} in the notation of Ref. [117], and Eq. (29) with these terms reproduces its Eqs. (50) and (51) term by term. The fixed line with U(1)×\timesSU(NN) flavor symmetry that follows from its Eq. (51) is gt=c−6​gAg_{t}=c-6g_{A} with z=1+(c−4​gA)/(2​π)z=1+(c-4g_{A})/(2\pi). A single random Dirac mass has the stable fixed point z∗=1+64/(3​π2​N)=1+2.16/Nz^{*}=1+64/(3\pi^{2}N)=1+2.16/N for NN two-component flavors; the random mass of Ref. [32] is a flavor non-singlet in two-component language, and its ϵ\epsilon-expansion value z∗=1+9​ϵ/(8​N4)z^{*}=1+9\epsilon/(8N_{4}) at ϵ=1\epsilon=1, with N4=N/2N_{4}=N/2 four-component flavors, equals 1+2.25/N1+2.25/N. In the SU(2) theory the triangle carries a single gauge generator and vanishes, and the two-gauge-line class requires tr⁡TX≠0\operatorname{tr}T_{X}\neq 0, which holds only for the 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd flux mass. The same normalization reproduces the annihilation value −64/(π2N)-64/(\pi^{2}N) of the flavor-singlet mass. A random potential on the U(1) gauge charge is screened at both replica ends, its correlator vanishing as k2k^{2}. Reference [32] dresses a single end and finds a correlator ∝|k|\propto|k| [its Eq. (C5)]; in both cases the random potential is irrelevant at the QED3 fixed point.

The kernel BB is the one of this appendix, and Eq. (30) follows from it on the invariant subspace {Δ+,Δ−,ΔJ}\{\Delta_{+},\Delta_{-},\Delta_{J}\}, with no weight generated outside it. A random 𝒯\mathcal{T}-even initial covariance generates no 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd and no gauge-charged entries, in accord with the per-replica selection rule. The times to strong disorder quoted in Sec. XII are those at which the largest class variance reaches π\pi; for vacancies the initial covariance is that of the near–far imbalance. The cell-correlated random λ\lambda generates no mass and stays marginally irrelevant, Eq. (27). At ℓ∗\ell^{*} the covariance is dominated by the two plaquette components with equal variance and the VBS-rotation current at half of it.

The Higgs dimensions follow from the same logarithms with the scalar propagator 1/p21/p^{2}, the gauge vertex (p+p′)μ​tb(p+p^{\prime})_{\mu}t^{b}, the seagull, and the constraint field with ⟨σ​σ⟩=16​|q|/M\langle\sigma\sigma\rangle=16|q|/M. For NN complex unit-charge scalars this gives ηN=1−32/(π2​N)\eta_{N}=1-32/(\pi^{2}N), the CPN-1 value of Ref. [53] (its Table I at d=3d=3). Vacancy at mean-field level. The Nambu Hamiltonian H=−∑ψi†ui​jψj+h.c.H=-\sum\psi_{i}^{\dagger}u_{ij}\psi_{j}+{\rm h.c.} of the π\pi-flux and reference Z3000 ansätze is number conserving in ψ=(f↑,f↓†)\psi=(f_{\uparrow},f_{\downarrow}^{\dagger}), so each state is a Slater determinant of ψ\psi, with Sz=(ψ†​ψ−1)/2S^{z}=(\psi^{\dagger}\psi-1)/2 and ⟨𝑺i⋅𝑺j⟩=14[(ni−1)(nj−1)−trGi​jGj​i]+RedetGi​j\langle\bm{S}_{i}\cdot\bm{S}_{j}\rangle=\tfrac{1}{4}[(n_{i}-1)(n_{j}-1)-\operatorname{tr}G_{ij}G_{ji}]+\operatorname{Re}\det G_{ij}, Gi​j=⟨ψi†​ψj⟩G_{ij}=\langle\psi_{i}^{\dagger}\psi_{j}\rangle. A vacancy removes one site and its bonds on clusters of (2​L)2(2L)^{2} sites, L=6L=6–1616, with antiperiodic and open boundaries. The zero-field state is the average of the two members of the Kramers doublet, in which the pair of ψ\psi modes closest to zero energy is filled or left empty, Sz=±1/2S^{z}=\pm 1/2. In the π\pi-flux state (−1)x+y(-1)^{x+y} anticommutes with HH and the removed site leaves an index of two, matched by two zero modes at every size and for both boundaries, with weight below 10−2810^{-28} on the vacancy sublattice. The weight inside r≤2r\leq 2 and r≤4r\leq 4 follows 1/W=a​ln⁡L+b1/W=a\ln L+b with residuals below 10−310^{-3} (antiperiodic) and 10−210^{-2} (open). The bond-energy response δ​e\delta e on nearest-neighbor bonds is projected on the lattice harmonics of the zero-gradient channels, Vx=∑x(−1)x​δ​eV_{x}=\sum_{x}(-1)^{x}\delta e and Vy=∑y(−1)y​δ​eV_{y}=\sum_{y}(-1)^{y}\delta e, with P∓=Vx±VyP_{\mp}=V_{x}\pm V_{y} for the full and empty plaquette, and the staggered harmonics (−1)x+y(-1)^{x+y} for the VBS-rotation current, whose signs follow from the zero-mode projection of single bonds. With antiperiodic boundaries every harmonic is below 10−1410^{-14} and the pattern is invariant under C4C_{4} and the site mirror to 10−1510^{-15}; on open clusters, where the vacancy sits half a site from the center, the local harmonics decrease as 1/L1/L together with the C4C_{4} residual. Relaxing the amplitudes of all interdimer and dimer bonds within r≤3r\leq 3 self-consistently, with the bulk fixed at the π\pi-flux saddle, keeps C4​vC_{4v} to 10−1410^{-14} and the dimer amplitudes at zero. In the Z3000 state the chiral operator is (−1)x+y​τz(-1)^{x+y}\tau^{z}, with τz\tau^{z} acting on the Nambu index, whose trace over a site vanishes, and the pair of ψ\psi modes closest to zero energy splits by 1.8×10−31.8\times 10^{-3} to 1.2×10−11.2\times 10^{-1}, depending on size and boundary twist, while the Kramers doublet stays degenerate. For individual twists that break the site mirror the empty-plaquette harmonic reaches 1.3×10−31.3\times 10^{-3}; for diagonal twists and after averaging over 4×44\times 4 twists it is below 10−1510^{-15}, as the site mirror requires. Within r≤3r\leq 3 the twist-averaged full plaquette is 1.0×10−21.0\times 10^{-2}, 6.8×10−36.8\times 10^{-3}, 7.1×10−37.1\times 10^{-3} and 6.1×10−36.1\times 10^{-3} and the current −4.9×10−3-4.9\times 10^{-3} to −3.3×10−3-3.3\times 10^{-3} for L=6L=6–1212; the extrapolation of the full plaquette in 1/L1/L stays finite, (2CLOSE(2–OPEN6)×10−36)\times 10^{-3}, and both harmonics grow faster than linearly with the Z3000 amplitudes. The 𝒯\mathcal{T}-odd observables, the magnetization and the scalar chirality on the triangles of the sixteen plaquettes around the vacancy, are below 10−1410^{-14} in the 𝒯\mathcal{T}-invariant state in every case.

Appendix H Induced gauge propagator: the adjoint-Higgs polarization

The critical theory carries no Maxwell term. The gauge propagator is generated entirely by matter loops, so the count N=2​Nf+4​NbN=2N_{f}+4N_{b} of Sec. III and the propagator Dμ​νD_{\mu\nu} that Appendix O takes as input are themselves computed quantities. The fermions of each valley form one complex two-component Dirac gauge doublet with covariant derivative Dμ=∂μ−iAaμσaD_{\mu}=\partial_{\mu}-\mathrm{i}A^{a}_{\mu}\sigma^{a} and bare vertex γμ​σa\gamma_{\mu}\sigma^{a}, so that tr⁡σa​σb=2​δa​b\operatorname{tr}\sigma^{a}\sigma^{b}=2\delta^{ab}. The Higgs fields are real adjoint triplets with (Dμ​Φ)a=∂μΦa−i​Aμb​(tb)a​c​Φc(D_{\mu}\Phi)_{a}=\partial_{\mu}\Phi_{a}-\mathrm{i}A^{b}_{\mu}(t^{b})_{ac}\Phi_{c} and (tb)a​c=−2​i​ϵb​a​c(t^{b})_{ac}=-2\mathrm{i}\epsilon_{bac}, so that tr⁡(ta​tb)=8​δa​b\operatorname{tr}(t^{a}t^{b})=8\delta^{ab}. The one-loop polarization is transverse and reads

Πμ​νa​b​(p)=δa​b​(δμ​ν−pμ​pνp2)​(2​Nf+4​Nb)​|p|16.\Pi^{ab}_{\mu\nu}(p)=\delta^{ab}\Bigl(\delta_{\mu\nu}-\frac{p_{\mu}p_{\nu}}{p^{2}}\Bigr)\frac{(2N_{f}+4N_{b})\,|p|}{16}. (39)

The two weights arise as follows. A two-component Dirac fermion of unit charge screens with |p|/16|p|/16 (Appendix O), and the doublet loop with two Pauli vertices multiplies this by tr⁡σa​σb=2​δa​b\operatorname{tr}\sigma^{a}\sigma^{b}=2\delta^{ab}, giving weight 2 per valley. Writing a valley as eight real Majorana components (Appendix B) does not change this weight: realification doubles the trace to 44 and the Majorana loop halves it back to 22. A complex scalar of unit charge also screens with |p|/16|p|/16 (Appendix O). A real adjoint triplet integrates to 12​Tr⁡log\tfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{Tr}\log, so its weight is 12​tr⁡(ta​tb)=4\tfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}(t^{a}t^{b})=4 per triplet. The critical sector contains the two real triplets Φ1,Φ2\Phi_{1},\Phi_{2}, hence Nb=2N_{b}=2 real triplets and N=2​Nf+4​Nb=4+8=12N=2N_{f}+4N_{b}=4+8=12.

Two limits fix the fermion weight independently. In the U(1) sublimit in which only Aμ3A^{3}_{\mu} is kept, σ3=±1\sigma^{3}=\pm 1 on the two doublet components, so each valley contributes two unit-charge two-component fermions and Π33=2​Nf​|p|/16=4​|p|/16\Pi^{33}=2N_{f}|p|/16=4|p|/16, the N=4N=4 QED3 that is the standard count for the π\pi-flux Dirac spin liquid. The companion U(1) analysis of Ref. [26] uses the same rule, Πa=(Nf+4​Nb)​|p|/16\Pi_{a}=(N_{f}+4N_{b})|p|/16 in its notation. There each two-component fermion carries weight 1, with Nf=4N_{f}=4 for its triangular and kagome theories and Nf=12N_{f}=12 for its maple-leaf theory, and each complex charge-2 scalar carries weight 4. Reference [27] uses the same count, ΠA=(2​Nf+4​Nb)​|p|/16\Pi_{A}=(2N_{f}+4N_{b})|p|/16 in its Eq. (64). Inverting Eq. (39) gives Dμ​ν=16N​|q|​(δμ​ν−ζ​q^μ​q^ν)D_{\mu\nu}=\frac{16}{N|q|}(\delta_{\mu\nu}-\zeta\hat{q}_{\mu}\hat{q}_{\nu}) and hence dim[ψ¯​μi​ψ]=2−64/(π2​N)=1.46\dim[\bar{\psi}\mu^{i}\psi]=2-64/(\pi^{2}N)=1.46 at N=12N=12 (Sec. VII). The O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) correction to Eq. (39), comprising two-loop matter blocks, a ghost loop, and the induced three-gauge-boson vertex class generated by matter triangles, is what an O⁡(1/N2)O(1/N^{2}) determination of ΔV\Delta_{V} would require. It is not evaluated here.

Appendix I DM-induced Yukawa couplings

Scaling dimensions. At the SO(5)- and Lorentz-invariant point the γ0\gamma^{0} channel of Eq. (10), Φ1,2a​Tr​[σa​𝒳¯​μy​σb​γ0​𝒳]\Phi_{1,2}^{a}\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mu^{y}\sigma^{b}\gamma^{0}\mathcal{X}], and the Yukawa coupling yy of Ref. [27], Φ1,2a​Tr​[σa​𝒳¯​μz,x​γx,y​𝒳]\Phi_{1,2}^{a}\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mu^{z,x}\gamma^{x,y}\mathcal{X}], are components of the same multiplet, SO(5) vector times Lorentz vector times gauge adjoint, and have the same dimension to all orders. The scalar channel Φ1,2a​Tr​[σa​𝒳¯​𝒳​σb]\Phi_{1,2}^{a}\mathrm{Tr}[\sigma^{a}\bar{\mathcal{X}}\mathcal{X}\sigma^{b}] has the Dirac structure 𝟙\mathds{1}. Reference [27] evaluates the two vertex graphs for a Yukawa vertex with and without Dirac structure [its Eqs. (97)–(99)], and its Eq. (100) gives at Nf=Nb=2N_{f}=N_{b}=2 the RG eigenvalues 1.3781.378 for Γ∝γμ\Gamma\propto\gamma^{\mu}, which includes yy, and 1.1981.198 for Γ∝𝟙\Gamma\propto\mathds{1}; the scalar DM channel is of the second type. The following evaluation corroborates their difference. The fermion and Higgs self-energies do not depend on the Dirac structure Γ\Gamma of the vertex. In the graph with the gauge line on the Higgs leg a single fermion propagator separates the two vertices, and the Higgs–gauge vertex qνq_{\nu} contracts with the adjacent γμ\gamma_{\mu}, γμ​q̸​Γ​qν​(δμ​ν−ζ​qμ​qν/q2)=(1−ζ)​q2​Γ\gamma_{\mu}\not{q}\,\Gamma\,q_{\nu}(\delta_{\mu\nu}-\zeta q_{\mu}q_{\nu}/q^{2})=(1-\zeta)q^{2}\Gamma, so this graph is the same for every Γ\Gamma. In the graph joining the two fermion legs, in d=3d=3 with 2×22\times 2 Dirac matrices, γμ​q̸​Γ​q̸​γμ\gamma_{\mu}\not{q}\Gamma\not{q}\gamma_{\mu} averages to q2​Γ/3q^{2}\Gamma/3 for Γ=γν\Gamma=\gamma^{\nu} and to 3​q2​Γ3q^{2}\Gamma for Γ=𝟙\Gamma=\mathds{1}, and the gauge-adjoint color factor is σb​σa​σb=−σa\sigma^{b}\sigma^{a}\sigma^{b}=-\sigma^{a}. In units u=8/(3​π2​N)u=8/(3\pi^{2}N), this graph gives (1−3​ζ)​u(1-3\zeta)u for γν\gamma^{\nu} and (9−3​ζ)​u(9-3\zeta)u for 𝟙\mathds{1}, so

Δscalar−Δy=8​u=643​N​π2,\Delta_{\rm scalar}-\Delta_{y}=8u=\frac{64}{3N\pi^{2}}, (40)

gauge independent. Triplet amplitudes allowed by the locked PSG. We parametrize every translation-invariant real antisymmetric Majorana form AA, with H=i​∑K​LAK​L​MK​MLH=\mathrm{i}\sum_{KL}A_{KL}M_{K}M_{L}, on the NN (8 per cell), dimer (2), orthogonal-dimer (2), empty-square-diagonal (4) and on-site (4) classes by 4×44\times 4 bond blocks. This gives 16×16+4×6=28016\times 16+4\times 6=280 real parameters covering both spins and both Majorana components, hence all hoppings and pairings, singlet and triplet. A locked generator acts on the four Majoranas of a site through the real orthogonal matrix induced by the PSG gauge WOW_{O} on the Nambu doublets and by the axial spin rotation ΩO\Omega_{O} on (f↑,f↓)(f_{\uparrow},f_{\downarrow}), generated by the lattice spin operators of Appendix D. The construction follows the spin–orbit-locked PSG of Ref. [23], which kept only zz-component triplets on the kagome lattice. Here it is extended to all three triplet components and to the spin rotations that accompany the operations of the SS space group, and it is written in Majorana form. As in Ref. [23], the 𝒯\mathcal{T} generator is the antiunitary spin flip combined with an additional gauge rotation, here W𝒯​i​τyW_{\mathcal{T}}\mathrm{i}\tau^{y}. Reference [27] writes its ansätze in Wen’s Nambu formalism [126] and gives its time-reversal PSG element in its Eq. (A.7). In that formalism 𝒯\mathcal{T} acts as ui​j→ui​j∗u_{ij}\to u_{ij}^{*}, which with Wen’s fixed gauge rotation −i​τ2-\mathrm{i}\tau^{2} becomes ui​j→−ui​ju_{ij}\to-u_{ij} [his Eq. (19)] before the PSG element is applied. In Wen’s variables this is the operation above. The generator W𝒯​i​τyW_{\mathcal{T}}\mathrm{i}\tau^{y} leaves both the Z3000 ansatz and the Wick-induced DM operators invariant, whereas W𝒯W_{\mathcal{T}} without the i​τy\mathrm{i}\tau^{y} does not act correctly on triplets. The allowed ansatz is the common fixed space of {T2​x,T2​y,Gx​σh⊗C2​x,σx​y⊗C2(1,−1,0),𝒯}\{T_{2x},T_{2y},G_{x}\sigma_{h}\otimes C_{2x},\sigma_{xy}\otimes C_{2}^{(1,-1,0)},\mathcal{T}\} (buckled) or of {T2​x,T2​y,Gx⊗C2​y,σx​y⊗C2(1,−1,0),σh⊗C2​z,𝒯,U​(1)z}\{T_{2x},T_{2y},G_{x}\otimes C_{2y},\sigma_{xy}\otimes C_{2}^{(1,-1,0)},\sigma_{h}\otimes C_{2z},\mathcal{T},{\rm U(1)}_{z}\} (high-temperature), split into singlets and triplets by the global spin rotations. With trivial spin factors and full spin SU(2) the fixed space consists of seven singlet amplitudes (two NN, one dimer, one orthogonal, two empty-square, one on-site), and it contains no triplet. The Z3000 ansatz of Ref. [27], Eqs. (8)–(17) there, lies inside it. That ansatz has six real parameters and no on-site term, so it accounts for six of the seven amplitudes. With the locked generators the singlet space is unchanged, and the Wick-induced DM operators (in-plane inter-dimer, intra-dimer and D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp}) lie inside the fixed space and are purely triplet. The triplet complement is the orthogonal complement of the singlet space within the allowed space. The buckled structure admits 14 triplet amplitudes, block-diagonal by bond class with 6 (NN), 2 (dimer), 2 (orthogonal), 4 (empty-square) and 0 (on-site). The high-temperature structure admits 2 triplet amplitudes, both on NN bonds.

Fixed-background stability of the DM mean fields. The analysis covers the in-plane staggered inter-dimer channel only, with the Z3000(sH)(s_{H}) singlet amplitudes held fixed, at sH=0.05s_{H}=0.05 and 0.10.1 with d=0.6d=0.6. The ansatz form is that of Ref. [27], Eqs. (8)–(17) there. The amplitudes form a one-parameter family fixed by hand and are not obtained variationally. In the notation of Ref. [27] they are t=1t=1, θ=π/2+0.30​sH\theta=\pi/2+0.30\,s_{H}, Δd=0.40​sH\Delta_{d}=0.40\,s_{H}, Δd′=0.25​sH\Delta_{d^{\prime}}=0.25\,s_{H}, Δg,1=0.15​sH\Delta_{g,1}=0.15\,s_{H} and Δg,2=0.10​sH\Delta_{g,2}=0.10\,s_{H}. The same family underlies every Z3000(sH)(s_{H}) result in this paper. The lattice is the 8×88\times 8-cell torus with periodic boundary conditions, on which the Z3000(sH)(s_{H}) state has a finite-size gap (minimum excitation energy 0.0470.047 at sH=0.05s_{H}=0.05, 0.0950.095 at 0.10.1). The Wick decoupling of HDMH_{\rm DM} on the ground state of Z3000(sH)(s_{H})+d​hDM(n)d\,h^{(n)}_{\rm DM} defines hDM(n+1)h^{(n+1)}_{\rm DM}. Starting from the Wick operator h(0)h^{(0)} of Appendix D, the iteration converges geometrically in a few steps. Relative to h(0)h^{(0)} the converged operator has its norm changed by 0.06%0.06\% (0.04%0.04\%) and its direction rotated by 4.4∘4.4^{\circ} (4.3∘4.3^{\circ}) for sH=0.05s_{H}=0.05 (0.10.1). It lies inside the locked-PSG-allowed space, with 99.4%99.4\% of its squared norm triplet and 0.6%0.6\% singlet. The NN singlet amplitude moves from 0.23910.2391 to 0.23860.2386, δ′\delta^{\prime} from 0.005480.00548 to 0.005490.00549 (0.02120→0.021260.02120\to 0.02126), and the nodes of the Bloch spectrum stay gapless. This establishes the stability of one channel on a fixed background; it is not a self-consistent solution of the full DM-coupled ansatz.

Appendix K Tree-level quartic seeds

At zeroth order in gradients the parton fields of the 2×22\times 2 cell reduce to the Γ\Gamma-point modes of the π\pi-flux state, fs​σ=∑d,vbs,(d,v)​cd​v​σf_{s\sigma}=\sum_{d,v}b_{s,(d,v)}c_{dv\sigma}, with the orthogonal basis map bb of Eq. (26) of Ref. [27] (Dirac index dd, valley index vv, sublattice ss). The eight complex modes cd​v​σc_{dv\sigma} are represented on their full 282^{8}-dimensional Fock space. The spin operators 𝑺s=12​fs†​𝝈​fs\bm{S}_{s}=\frac{1}{2}f_{s}^{\dagger}\bm{\sigma}f_{s} are built from them, and the exchange operators of Eq. (1) per cell are formed with two dimer bonds and eight nearest-neighbor bonds. Running between the lattice scale and λ\lambda. The Dirac-regime dimensions are computed in the Majorana basis of the sixteen Γ\Gamma-point modes, with the kinetic matrices of the continuum limit, the gauge generators in the same basis, and the propagator and angular averages of Eqs. (49) and (52). A local operator with nn legs and coefficient tensor TT has Δ=Δtree−Ex−n2​cS+Aann\Delta=\Delta_{\rm tree}-E_{\rm x}-\tfrac{n}{2}c_{S}+A_{\rm ann}, where cSc_{S} is the self-energy coefficient, ExE_{\rm x} the sum over all pairs of legs of the one-gauge-line exchange, and AannA_{\rm ann} the two-gauge-line annihilation of a pair of legs, Fig. 7(a)–(c). The annihilation of an arbitrary pair, obtained from the fermion triangle at zero pair momentum, acts in two channels only. The triangle gives the flux-singlet pair the lifting of Eq. (17). The SO(5)-singlet gauge-current pairs JμcJ^{c}_{\mu} annihilate through the induced three-gauge vertex. At zero pair momentum the Ward identity fixes this vertex to 4​Nf​εc​a​b​∂λΠ1μ​ν​(q)4N_{f}\varepsilon^{cab}\,\partial_{\lambda}\Pi_{1}^{\mu\nu}(q), with Π1\Pi_{1} the polarization of one two-component Majorana fermion. Onto a fermion line it gives −(3−2ζ)/9-(3-2\zeta)/9 of the lifting in gauge ζ\zeta, and onto a Higgs line a longitudinal part equal to the gauge-dependent part of the fermion line. By the gauge-field equation of motion Jψ+JΦ=0J_{\psi}+J_{\Phi}=0 the two combine into the gauge-independent shift −19⋅16/(3π2)=−128Nf/(3π2N2)-\tfrac{1}{9}\cdot 16/(3\pi^{2})=-128N_{f}/(3\pi^{2}N^{2}) per current pair. For n=2n=2 these rules give the self-energy coefficient of Eq. (54) for every gauge parameter, Δ=2\Delta=2 for all thirty current components, Δ=2−64/(π2​N)=1.4596\Delta=2-64/(\pi^{2}N)=1.4596 for the five SO(5)-vector masses and Δ=2\Delta=2 for the flux singlet, Eq. (17). The fermion loop they imply carries the factor 2​Nf2N_{f} of the polarization. Two countings of the annihilation are used. In the leading large-NfN_{f} counting only pairs of legs whose loop carries a free valley trace annihilate. In the physical-NfN_{f} counting, used for the spectrum and for Table 9, every pair of legs annihilates with its actual loop factor at Nf=2N_{f}=2, which includes Fierz-crossed pairs that are formally O⁡(1/N2)O(1/N^{2}). The leading counting gives, in the abelian version with four flavors, 4−64/(π2​N)4-64/(\pi^{2}N) and 4+64/(3​π2​N)4+64/(3\pi^{2}N) for the two Lorentz-scalar four-fermion operators with one field of each flavor, and 4+64​(2±7)/(3​π2​N)4+64(2\pm\sqrt{7})/(3\pi^{2}N) for the flavor-singlet pair (ψ¯​ψ)2(\bar{\psi}\psi)^{2}, (ψ¯​γμ​ψ)2(\bar{\psi}\gamma_{\mu}\psi)^{2}, the values of Refs. [129, 15] [Eqs. (1.3) and (1.7) of Ref. [15], which obtains the singlet pair from the mixing of (ψ¯​ψ)2(\bar{\psi}\psi)^{2} with Fμ​ν​Fμ​νF_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu} and quotes 4+64/(3​π2​N)4+64/(3\pi^{2}N) from Sec. II.C of Ref. [129]], as well as the normalization-independent entries of the U(1) flow of Ref. [129], its Eq. (6); the physical-NfN_{f} counting gives 4+(−25.3,+94.6)/(π2​N)4+(-25.3,+94.6)/(\pi^{2}N) for that pair instead of 4+(−13.8,+99.1)/(π2​N)4+(-13.8,+99.1)/(\pi^{2}N). In QED3 the current square stands in for F2F^{2}: the gauge-field equation of motion makes it redundant, and its Wilsonian coupling carries the O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) mixing of F2F^{2} (Fig. 7(d)), so that mixing is included. The two countings differ only in the SO(5) representations 11, 55 and 1010, by 0.120.12 in the lowest singlet of the four-fermion block (2.4772.477 against 2.5922.592) and by less than 0.030.03 elsewhere; we quote the physical-NfN_{f} values and regard the difference as part of the O⁡(1/N2)O(1/N^{2}) uncertainty. On the 336 gauge-invariant four-fermion operators the dimension operator is independent of the gauge parameter to 10−1410^{-14}, self-adjoint in the free-field metric and SO(5) covariant. Its eigenvalues are 2.4772.477, 3.2193.219, 3.4053.405, 3.4603.460, 3.8203.820, 3.8503.850, 3.9103.910, 44, 4.2024.202, 4.2054.205 and 4.5404.540. Mixing with operators that contain gauge or Higgs fields, which have the same dimension at N=∞N=\infty, can only occur in the SO(5) representations 11, 55 and 1010. Among the channel-carrying eigenspaces of Table 9 this affects only the SO(5) singlets. The eigenvalue 44 of the 3535 Lorentz vector, which carries the D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} plaquette selector, has no anomalous term for the following reasons. The 3535 Lorentz vector occurs once among the 336 operators, so it cannot mix. It contains no flux-singlet and no gauge-current pair, so no annihilation graph contributes (below 10−1710^{-17}). It lies in the span of products of two SO(5) currents (to 10−1510^{-15}), and on it the gauge exchanges between legs of different currents sum to zero. The self-energy and the exchanges within each current then cancel by the Ward identity, for every gauge parameter: the self-energy is +0.135+0.135 at ζ=0\zeta=0 and −0.270-0.270 at ζ=1\zeta=1, and the exchanges are the negatives. The 1414 spin-2 eigenspace, also a pure current product, behaves in the same way. No symmetry argument for the cancellation between different currents is known, and it does not hold in general: the 35′35^{\prime} scalar, also a pure current product, receives +64/(π2N)=0.54+64/(\pi^{2}N)=0.54. The value 44 is therefore an O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) statement.

The dimension of Fa​FaF^{a}F^{a} with Higgs loops. At the multicritical point the gauge field is screened by the fermions and by the adjoint Higgs triplets, and the dimension of Fa​FaF^{a}F^{a} receives Higgs-loop contributions absent from Ref. [34]. It follows from adding a Maxwell term (ϵ/4)​Fa​Fa(\epsilon/4)F^{a}F^{a} to the fixed point and extracting the logarithms of the O⁡(1/N)O(1/N) gluon two-point function, Γ2=Π0​(1+βb​L)+ϵ​q2​PT​(1+βc​L)\Gamma_{2}=\Pi_{0}(1+\beta_{b}L)+\epsilon q^{2}P_{T}(1+\beta_{c}L) with L=ln⁡(Λ/|q|)L=\ln(\Lambda/|q|), so that Δ⁡(Fa​Fa)=4−βc+βb\Delta(F^{a}F^{a})=4-\beta_{c}+\beta_{b}. The gluon field renormalization βb\beta_{b} follows from the fermion self-energy and the vertex correction through the induced three-gluon vertex, fixed at zero momentum by the Ward identity. The coefficient βc\beta_{c} collects the box, the two-triangle and the cubic-Maxwell diagrams built from the matter-induced vertices and, for critical Higgs fields, the exchange of the constraint field between two induced A​A​σAA\sigma vertices. Every induced vertex is expanded by regions in the soft external momentum. Only the hard regions, in which all loop momenta are of the order of the internal gluon momentum, renormalize Fa​FaF^{a}F^{a} into itself; the soft regions, in which a matter loop carries the external momentum, are the mixing of Fa​FaF^{a}F^{a} into matter operators, above all the redundant square of the total current, and drop out of the diagonal entry. The prescription agrees with the three published values: 4+320/(3​π2​N)4+320/(3\pi^{2}N) for fermionic SU(2) screening [34] (computed there in Landau gauge) in every covariant gauge, the vanishing diagonal of fermionic QED3 [15], and 4+32/(3​π2​N)4+32/(3\pi^{2}N) for the critical CPN-1 model [Eq. (27) of Ref. [120] at d=3d=3], which the hard and soft regions together would miss by a factor of two. With xbx_{b} the Higgs share of the screening and xf=1−xbx_{f}=1-x_{b},

for critical Higgs fields, and without the last term for Gaussian ones, i.e. ΓF​F≡Δ⁡(Fa​Fa)=5.14\Gamma_{FF}\equiv\Delta(F^{a}F^{a})=5.14 (4.984.98) at N=12N=12, independent of the gauge parameter. Two pieces have no published benchmark: the fermion–Higgs cross term, corroborated by a direct extraction from the full triangle, and the non-abelian part of the critical-scalar sector, which the abelian CPN-1 total cannot separate. Replacing 5.145.14 by the Gaussian-Higgs value 4.984.98, or by the value 4.904.90 that the hard and soft regions together give in Feynman gauge (ζ=0\zeta=0), moves the lowest four-fermion singlet below by less than 10−310^{-3}. Appendix N Monopole operators of the U800 state

At the SU(2) point the gauge flux is not conserved and there is no monopole operator. The SO(5) vector of Néel and VBS order parameters consists of fermion bilinears [125], and these are classified in Sec. IV. In Z3000 the gauge group is ℤ2\mathbb{Z}_{2}. In U800, ⟨Φ3⟩≠0\langle\Phi_{3}\rangle\neq 0 breaks SU(2) to U(1), and the low-energy theory is compact QED3 with four two-component Dirac fermions. A monopole operator inserts 2​π2\pi flux. Each Dirac cone then contributes one zero mode, and gauge neutrality fills two of the four, which gives six monopoles. They decompose as 6=1⊕56=1\oplus 5 under the SO(5) of the parent theory [110, 125]: an SO(5) singlet and a vector made of two spin-singlet (VBS-like) and three spin-triplet (Néel-like) operators. The action of the lattice symmetries on them includes a phase in the flux (topological) U(1). This phase is not contained in the PSG and has to be computed [110, 111].

In the U800 PSG [Eq. (A.4) of Ref. [27]] the translations have gauge part only in the U(1) invariant gauge group, while GxG_{x} and σx​y\sigma_{xy} carry a τ1\tau^{1}-type gauge part that reverses the U(1) charge. Both operations also reverse orientation, so they preserve the sign of the U(1) flux. So does 𝒯\mathcal{T}, which maps ui​j​ei​Ai​j​τ3u_{ij}e^{iA_{ij}\tau^{3}} to −ui​j​ei​Ai​j​τ3-u_{ij}e^{iA_{ij}\tau^{3}} before its gauge part, which commutes with τ3\tau^{3}, is applied. Every element therefore maps monopoles to monopoles. An antiunitary element that sends a monopole MM to ei​φ​Me^{i\varphi}M only fixes the phase of gMg_{M} in gM​M+h.c.g_{M}M+{\rm h.c.}, so a monopole is symmetry-allowed if and only if it is invariant under the unitary elements.

The monopole representation follows from inserting 2​π2\pi flux into the U800 mean-field state, ui​j→ui​j​ei​Ai​j​τ3u_{ij}\to u_{ij}e^{iA_{ij}\tau^{3}}, on an Lt×LtL_{t}\times L_{t} torus (Lt=2​LL_{t}=2L) with flux 2​π/Lt22\pi/L_{t}^{2} per plaquette. A symmetry gg acts on Nambu modes through its PSG. In the flux sector it is combined with the gauge transformation that restores AA, lifted to Fock space as exp⁡(i​∑iϑi​Qi)\exp(i\sum_{i}\vartheta_{i}Q_{i}) with Qi=ψi†​τ3​ψiQ_{i}=\psi_{i}^{\dagger}\tau^{3}\psi_{i}, which acts trivially on Gutzwiller-projected states. Each eigenvalue is taken relative to that of the zero-flux ground state with the same lift. A single flux quantum on a torus is invariant only under point operations that share a fixed point. We therefore use two geometries. The first is C4C_{4} about the center of an empty square, with holonomies (π+π/Lt,π−3​π/Lt)(\pi+\pi/L_{t},\pi-3\pi/L_{t}). The second is {σx​y,σx​y¯,C2}\{\sigma_{xy},\sigma_{x\bar{y}},C_{2}\} about a dimer center, with holonomies (π+π/Lt,π−π/Lt)(\pi+\pi/L_{t},\pi-\pi/L_{t}). The zero-flux reference has holonomies (π,π)(\pi,\pi) and is gapped, whereas periodic boundary conditions keep Dirac zero modes. The characters of GxG_{x} and of the translations follow from the relations σx​y​C4=T(−2,2)​Gx\sigma_{xy}C_{4}=T_{(-2,2)}G_{x} and Gx2=T2​xG_{x}^{2}=T_{2x}.

For L=3L=3 to 66 and flux angles θ\theta between 0.80.8 and 2.42.4 (the π\pi-flux point is θ=π/2\theta=\pi/2) the results do not change. The flux sector has two zero modes per spin, separated from the rest of the spectrum. The spin-triplet monopoles transform with a single character η\eta. The three spin singlets have eigenvalues {+1,+1,−1}\{+1,+1,-1\} under C4C_{4} and under each mirror, which fixes the SO(5)-singlet character χ1\chi_{1} as the repeated value. The two VBS monopoles ΦV±\Phi_{V\pm} are identified directly. A hopping modulation with the symmetry of the VBS mass V∓V_{\mp} splits the zero modes and leaves exactly one spin-singlet monopole at zero energy, ΦV±\Phi_{V\pm}, and its eigenvalue under the preserved element is then read off. Table 10 lists the results.

The SO(5)-singlet monopole is invariant under the full unlocked group. For symmetries under which the Higgs field is even, this is the statement of Ref. [110] that a U(1) state with an SU(2) parent has a symmetric monopole. Here it also holds for GxG_{x} and σx​y\sigma_{xy}, under which Φ3\Phi_{3} is odd and the U(1) charge is conjugated. The VBS and triplet monopoles carry the same signs as the VBS and Néel mass rows of Table 2. Neither is invariant, and spin rotations exclude the triplet in any case. The locked group adds an axial spin rotation to each element [Eq. (6)]. The spin singlets do not feel it, so the SO(5) singlet remains allowed and the VBS monopoles remain forbidden. On the triplet, S^4\hat{S}_{4} acts as η(C4)Rz(−π/2)=−Rz(−π/2)\eta(C_{4})R_{z}(-\pi/2)=-R_{z}(-\pi/2), with eigenvalues −1,±i-1,\pm i, so no spin direction is invariant. The same holds for the high-temperature locked group and for D⟂′D^{\prime}_{\perp} alone. DM therefore neither adds nor removes a symmetry-allowed monopole.

U800 thus carries one symmetry-allowed monopole, with or without DM. The symmetry argument excludes local masses in U800 but not confinement by monopole proliferation. Compact QED3 with the SO(5)-singlet monopole is a Higgs descendant of the SU(2) theory and shares its anomaly and its possible infrared behaviors [125]. The leading monopole of QED3 with four two-component flavors has scaling dimension 0.265×4≃1.060.265\times 4\simeq 1.06 at leading large-NfN_{f} order [6] and 1.021.02 with the O⁡(Nf0)O(N_{f}^{0}) correction [91], far below 33, so the allowed SO(5)-singlet monopole is expected to be strongly relevant and U800 to confine; its dimension in the present theory, with the DM couplings, is not computed here. The classification assumes that the leading monopoles form the six-dimensional vector and that the mean-field spinon state fixes their topological phases [110].

This appendix gives the rules and the integrals that underlie every large-NN number in the paper. The diagrams are those of Fig. 2, evaluated analytically with the gauge parameter ζ\zeta and the gauge factor CgC_{g} kept general.

i.e. Δsinglet−Δadj=−vann=+64/(π2N)\Delta_{\rm singlet}-\Delta_{\rm adj}=-v_{\rm ann}=+64/(\pi^{2}N), which is the QED3 value [47, 15, 3] [Eqs. (3.5), (3.6) of Ref. [3]]. The constant CtopoC_{\rm topo} follows from the count of distinct diagrams. A direct Wick expansion of the second-order term in the gauge coupling with the mass insertion on the loop produces exactly two distinct diagrams, the planar and the crossed attachment of the two gauge lines to the external fermion line, each with unit weight (the 4848 labeled contractions of this topology, 2424 planar and 2424 crossed, divided by the 4!4! of the vertex ordering). The four terms of the assembly above, two loop orientations times two orderings, therefore count each diagram twice, which is the magnitude 1/21/2. The sign follows from momentum conservation on the fermion line: with the gauge momentum ℓ\ell routed through the line, its propagator between the two attachments is G(k−ℓ)→−ℓ̸^/|ℓ|G(k-\ell)\to-\hat{\not{\ell}}/|\ell| at the logarithmic scale, opposite to the G⁡(+q)G(+q) written above. Both the magnitude and the sign follow from the Euclidean Feynman rules alone, and the result agrees with the abelian literature value. For the present theory the group factors are as follows: the loop carries tr⁡(σa​σb)=2​δa​b\mathrm{tr}(\sigma^{a}\sigma^{b})=2\delta^{ab} per valley, summed over the NfN_{f} valleys, the line carries ∑aσa​σa=3\sum_{a}\sigma^{a}\sigma^{a}=3, and the propagators carry (16/N)2(16/N)^{2}, so that NN in the QED3 loop factor is replaced by 6​Nf6N_{f}. The loop trace is symmetric in a,ba,b for both orientations, so no εa​b​c\varepsilon_{abc} part contributes. This gives Δflux−ΔVBS=64π2​6​NfN2=163​π2≃0.54\Delta_{\rm flux}-\Delta_{\rm VBS}=\frac{64}{\pi^{2}}\frac{6N_{f}}{N^{2}}=\frac{16}{3\pi^{2}}\simeq 0.54 at Nf=2N_{f}=2, N=12N=12, Eq. (17). The VBS (valley-adjoint) and Néel loops are traceless and receive no such term. Two points of the literature bear on this class. To our knowledge the singlet value 2+128/(3​π2​N)2+128/(3\pi^{2}N) first appears in the 2007 Erratum [47] to Ref. [46], whose original appendix asserted equal singlet and adjoint dimensions. It is sometimes attributed [15] to Ref. [92], which computed only flavor-nonsinglet bilinears (the adjoint mass and conserved currents). The four-component large-NfN_{f} values of γm\gamma_{m} [33, 16] refer to a parity-even bilinear that is an SU(2​Nf2N_{f}) adjoint of two-component fermions in d=3d=3. They receive no annihilation contribution and are not singlet values.

In the same way a closed Higgs loop with gauge vertices aa and bb carries 12​∑tr⁡(ta​tb)=W​δa​b\tfrac{1}{2}\sum\mathrm{tr}(t^{a}t^{b})=W\delta^{ab}, summed over the triplets, with W=4​NbW=4N_{b} the Higgs part of N=2​Nf+4​NbN=2N_{f}+4N_{b}, and a Higgs line carries Cs=tb​tb=8C_{s}=t^{b}t^{b}=8 against Cg=3C_{g}=3.

With the full propagator G−1=p2−Σ∝p2​(1+η​L)G^{-1}=p^{2}-\Sigma\propto p^{2}(1+\eta L) and the amputated Φ⋅Φ\Phi\cdot\Phi vertex 1+v​L1+vL, L=log⁡(Λ/k)L=\log(\Lambda/k), the insertion Φ⋅Φ\Phi\cdot\Phi has dimension 1+η−v1+\eta-v. Since ⟨σ​σ⟩=Πσ−1\langle\sigma\sigma\rangle=\Pi_{\sigma}^{-1} and Πσ\Pi_{\sigma} is the two-point function of Φ⋅Φ\Phi\cdot\Phi,

Δσ=3−Δ⁡(Φ⋅Φ)=2+v−η.\Delta_{\sigma}=3-\Delta(\Phi\cdot\Phi)=2+v-\eta. (63)

The three classes of Fig. 8(a)–(c) give the following.

(a) Constraint-field exchange:

Σ\displaystyle\Sigma =−∫q⟨σσ⟩(q)GΦ(k+q),\displaystyle=-\int_{q}\langle\sigma\sigma\rangle(q)\,G_{\Phi}(k{+}q),
v​L\displaystyle vL =−∫q⟨σσ⟩(q)GΦ(k+q)2,\displaystyle=-\int_{q}\langle\sigma\sigma\rangle(q)\,G_{\Phi}(k{+}q)^{2},
ησ\displaystyle\eta_{\sigma} =83​π2​M,vσ=−8π2​M.\displaystyle=\frac{8}{3\pi^{2}M},\qquad v_{\sigma}=-\frac{8}{\pi^{2}M}. (64)

(b) One gauge line, with Vμ=(2​k+q)μV_{\mu}=(2k+q)_{\mu} (the seagull tadpole is scaleless):

Σ\displaystyle\Sigma =Cs​∫qVμ​Vν​Dμ​ν​(q)​GΦ​(k+q),\displaystyle=C_{s}\int_{q}V_{\mu}V_{\nu}D_{\mu\nu}(q)\,G_{\Phi}(k{+}q),
v​L\displaystyle vL =Cs​∫qVμ​Vν​Dμ​ν​(q)​GΦ​(k+q)2,\displaystyle=C_{s}\int_{q}V_{\mu}V_{\nu}D_{\mu\nu}(q)\,G_{\Phi}(k{+}q)^{2},
ηA\displaystyle\eta_{A} =−8​Cs​(5+3​ζ)3​π2​N,vA=−8​Cs​(ζ−1)π2​N,\displaystyle=-\frac{8C_{s}(5+3\zeta)}{3\pi^{2}N},\qquad v_{A}=-\frac{8C_{s}(\zeta-1)}{\pi^{2}N}, (65)

so that vA−ηA=64​Cs/(3​π2​N)v_{A}-\eta_{A}=64C_{s}/(3\pi^{2}N) for every ζ\zeta.

(c) Higgs-loop annihilation. On a closed Higgs loop the insertion acts as a mass term, and the loop with two gauge vertices and its seagull enters through the mass derivative of Table 11,

Πμ​ν(1)​(q)\displaystyle\Pi^{(1)}_{\mu\nu}(q) =∂m2∫p[(2​p+q)μ​(2​p+q)ν(p2+m2)​((p+q)2+m2)−2​δμ​νp2+m2]\displaystyle=\partial_{m^{2}}\!\int_{p}\Bigl[\frac{(2p+q)_{\mu}(2p+q)_{\nu}}{(p^{2}+m^{2})((p+q)^{2}+m^{2})}-\frac{2\delta_{\mu\nu}}{p^{2}+m^{2}}\Bigr]
=−δμ​ν−q^μ​q^ν4​|q|,\displaystyle=-\frac{\delta_{\mu\nu}-\hat{q}_{\mu}\hat{q}_{\nu}}{4|q|}, (66)

after the infrared term (δμ​ν−q^μ​q^ν)/(4​π​m)(\delta_{\mu\nu}-\hat{q}_{\mu}\hat{q}_{\nu})/(4\pi m) is removed; the longitudinal part vanishes identically. The two gauge lines end on the seagull of the external line, so that

vann=Cs​W​∫qtr⁡[D⁡(q)​Π(1)​(q)​D​(q)]=−64​W​Csπ2​N2.v_{\rm ann}=C_{s}W\!\int_{q}\mathrm{tr}\bigl[D(q)\Pi^{(1)}(q)D(q)\bigr]=-\frac{64\,WC_{s}}{\pi^{2}N^{2}}. (67)

Π(1)\Pi^{(1)} is transverse, so the ζ\zeta terms of both propagators drop.

The constraint field generates no further logarithm. The insertion on a Higgs loop coupled through two σ\sigma lines contains ∂m2\partial_{m^{2}} of the bubble arctan⁡(|q|/2​m)/(4​π​|q|)\arctan(|q|/2m)/(4\pi|q|), which has no hard part. The induced σ3\sigma^{3} vertex is the triangle

∫l1l2​(l+p)2​(l−q)2=18​|p|​|q|​|p+q|,\int_{l}\frac{1}{l^{2}(l+p)^{2}(l-q)^{2}}=\frac{1}{8|p||q||p+q|}, (68)

and a graph with two of them falls as 1/(|q|​|p+q|)1/(|q||p+q|) at large |q||q|, which has no |q|−3|q|^{-3} term after the angular average. Adding the three classes in Eq. (63) gives Eq. (31), Δσ=2−72​u=0.379\Delta_{\sigma}=2-72u=0.379 at M=6M=6, Cs=W=8C_{s}=W=8, N=12N=12. With ν≃1+Δσ−2\nu\simeq 1+\Delta_{\sigma}-2 the same rules give ν=1−32/(3​π2​M)\nu=1-32/(3\pi^{2}M) for Cs=0C_{s}=0 and 1−48/(π2​N)1-48/(\pi^{2}N) for CPN-1 (M=2​NM=2N, Cs=1C_{s}=1, W=NW=N for NN complex components).

O.7 Master integrals

The integrals are collected in Table 11. Its third and fourth rows are the polarization loops of Fig. 2(g),(h): a two-component Dirac fermion and a complex scalar of unit charge screen identically, |q|/16|q|/16, which with the color weights of Appendix H (2 per Dirac valley doublet, 4 per real adjoint triplet) gives Eq. (39) and hence the 16/(N​|q|)16/(N|q|) of Eq. (49).
